gm.title: Appearance
lines: A slender pale-amber flying insect about 2 inches long, with a straw-like body and nearly transparent wings.

gm.title: Special attacks mechanics
lines: Bite · Deals 1 damage. A human or non-burden animal saves vs. paralyzation or develops sore, swollen joints. The separate beast-of-burden rule causes back pain and weakness that prevents carrying loads or traveling far.
Recovery · A cure disease spell cures the effect. Without magical treatment it lasts about two weeks.

gm.title: Traits mechanics
lines: Fragile · Any hit destroys an individual. Normal or magical cold and fire can harm it. It drowns if submerged and prevented from getting out.

gm.title: Encounters mechanics
lines: Arrival at Adhal · The affected camels show symptoms on the second night of travel. A successful Desert Survival or Healing proficiency check identifies the cause. See Adventure Book p. 8.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Neutral, animal intelligence 1, morale 6. Uncommon, daytime, omnivorous, and encountered in groups of 6–60. The block gives each insect 1 HP.
The source gives a paralyzation save for people and other animals and gives no separate save in the beast-of-burden paragraph.
The second-night timing belongs to the camel encounter. The animal entry gives no general onset time.
TSR, Corsairs of the Great Sea (1994), unnumbered Monstrous Compendium leaf, p. 100.

gm.title: Habitats
lines: Membrane dome by the boiling lake

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An immense aquatic crab that guards Wave. The encounter gives no shell color or armor.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Claw · melee · +18 to hit · reach 15 ft. · 2d6+8
Full attack: two claws, each · melee · +18 to hit · reach 15 ft. · 2d6+8

gm.title: Special attacks and qualities mechanics
lines: Improved grab · After a claw hit, the crab can attempt a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. A successful check establishes a hold and lets it constrict.
Constrict · A successful grapple check deals 4d6+8 constrict damage.
Amphibious · The aquatic crab survives indefinitely on land.

gm.title: Encounters mechanics
lines: Wave guardian · The 107 HP crab attacks intruders in the membrane dome. While fighting it stays at least 5 feet from the walls whenever possible.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Neutral. Intelligence shown as a dash. Toughness as a bonus feat. Space and reach are both 15 feet.
White Plume Mountain (2005 D&D 3.5 revision), Area 17, pp. 20–21. The adventure prints this full advanced stat block on p. 21.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Movement · 6 squares (forest walk), climb 6, burrow 6, swim 6

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A mass of long, thorny vines that can blend into surrounding vegetation.

gm.title: Powers
lines: Poison Lash · Standard, at-will · +20 vs. Reflex · 1d8 + 6 plus ongoing 5 poison (save ends)
Foot Snare · Minor, at-will · +20 vs. Fortitude · 1d8 + 6 and prone
Lashing Vines · Standard, at-will · +20 vs. Reflex · 2d8 + 6, with additional effects against immobilized enemies

gm.title: Power details mechanics
lines: Poison Lash · Melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. Poison keyword.
Foot Snare · Reach 4 squares. A hit knocks the target prone.
Lashing Vines · Healing keyword. Close burst 4 against enemies. Each hit on an immobilized target deals an extra 1d8 damage and restores 5 HP to the vine.
Rapid Growth · Encounter power. When first bloodied, the vine spawns two Ambush Vine Shoots within 4 squares. They act immediately after the vine on its initiative count.
Sprout Vine · At-will minor action. The vine takes 10 damage and spawns one Ambush Vine Shoot within 4 squares. The shoot acts immediately after the vine on its initiative count.

gm.title: Ambush Vine Shoot mechanics
lines: Level 15 Minion Controller · Medium fey beast (plant), 300 XP. Initiative +14, Perception +14, tremorsense 20, AC 29, Fortitude 27, Reflex 30, Will 23. Speed 6 squares and burrow 6. It has 1 HP and takes no damage from a missed attack.
Wrapping Vines · Standard at-will melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. +20 vs. Fortitude. Hit for 12 damage and restrain the target (save ends).
Enwrap · Enemies adjacent to the shoot take a −2 penalty to saving throws against immobilized and restrained.
Ability scores and Stealth · Str 18, Dex 25, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 12. Stealth +19, or +24 in undergrowth, trees, or swamps. Unaligned. No languages.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: August 2012 update, p. 82, corrects the parent vine’s original 1,400 XP to 2,800 XP. The shoot’s 300 XP comes from its own block.
Unaligned. No languages. Saving throws +2 and one action point. Stealth rises from +20 to +25 in undergrowth, trees or swamp.
The vine stalks prey through canopy, soil and water. It can hide underground or blend with surrounding plants.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, Monster Manual 2 (4e), pp. 204–205, with the August 2012 Rules Update, p. 82.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Str +9, Dex +6. Acrobatics +10, Athletics +9, Perception +9. Resists cold and thunder. Immune to lightning. Passive Perception 19. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The ancient eel breathes air and water. It can remain out of water for up to 24 hours.
Foudroyant Majesty (3/day). Turn a failed save into a success. Doing so prevents the ancient eel from using Multiattack on its next turn.
Slippery. The eel has advantage on checks and saves to avoid or escape the Grappled condition.
Stormsurge. Each other Lightning Eel within 30 ft. deals an extra 4 (1d8) lightning damage with weapon attacks and Electric Pulse.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and use Electric Pulse.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing plus 9 (2d8) lightning damage and grapple the target (escape DC 17). The grappled target is Restrained. The ancient eel cannot bite another target while that grapple lasts.
Electric Pulse. One creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 16 Constitution save, with disadvantage if it is touching the ancient eel. On a failure, it takes 27 (6d8) lightning damage and is Dazed until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and avoids Dazed.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Coiling Storm. One creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. On a failure, the ancient eel grapples it (escape DC 17).

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Heart of the Storm. When another Lightning Eel the ancient eel can see within 30 ft. drops to 0 HP, restore it to life with 10 HP. An eel can benefit from this reaction only once.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Use each action once per encounter after an enemy’s turn. Take them in any order, with at most one per round.
Call to the Storm. Each other Lightning Eel within 30 ft. can use Electric Pulse as a reaction.
Electric Rush. Move up to the ancient eel’s speed, then make a Bite attack that deals an extra 18 (4d8) lightning damage on a hit. A creature that hits the ancient eel with a melee attack during this movement takes 9 (2d8) lightning damage.
Fulminous Wave. Use Electric Pulse against every enemy within 30 ft.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: A Dazed creature can do one of the following on its turn: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. If it becomes Dazed during its turn, the turn ends. Extra actions granted by effects such as Haste or Action Surge remain available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration remove the condition. The GM can allow other remedies.

gm.title: Appearance

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC 14 (−1 size, +2 Dex, +3 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 12. Base attack +3, grapple +12. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +2.

lines: Two claws +7 melee (1d6 + 5 each) and bite +2 melee (1d6 + 2).

gm.title: Special qualities
lines: Low-light vision doubles normal human sight distance in dim light and retains color and detail. Scent (Ex). Detects opponents within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind or 15 ft. downwind. Double the range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering ones. It takes a move action to learn the direction. Within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.

gm.title: Skills and feats

gm.title: Encounter ecology

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A broad-shouldered saber-toothed cat wearing fitted half-plate barding.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Specially fitted half plate. Perception +3, Stealth +6. Passive Perception 13. No languages.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Curse of Strahd, first printing, march 2016, Chapter 5, The Town of Vallaki, N5 Arasek Stockyard, p. 115. Inherits the Saber-Toothed Tiger stat block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 336. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cos/the-town-of-vallaki#AreasofVallaki

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Keen Smell. The tiger has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on scent.
Pounce. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hit it with Claw on that turn. The creature falls prone on a failed DC 14 Strength save. A prone target can then be bitten once as a bonus action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

gm.title: Encounter application
lines: The tiger was trained to hunt Vistani servants of Strahd, per the p. 115 erratum. If released, it can track Rictavio or Piccolo by scent. Rictavio can stop an attack and coax it into the wagon. During the Tyger, Tyger event on pp. 123–124, it roams until hurt, then attacks the perceived source of the harm.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Rictavio keeps the tiger in his carnival wagon in Vallaki and feeds it through the roof hatch.

gm.title: Source notes
lines:
The first printing replaces the base armor, HP, and challenge. It gives 84 HP without a replacement Hit Dice formula.
The printed base block gives +6 to hit and +5 damage on both attacks. The adventure does not change either value.
Publisher errata changes p. 115 to target Strahd’s Vistani servants and removes recognition by scent and clothing from that paragraph. Page 116 of the first printing describes broader targeting and is not separately amended in the errata.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC 16 (+4 size, +2 Dexterity), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Base attack +2, grapple none. Space 10 ft., reach 0 ft.

gm.title: Attack
lines: Swarm. Automatically deal 1d6 damage to each creature whose space the swarm occupies at the end of its move. There is no attack roll or miss chance from cover or concealment.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Swarm. Automatically deal 1d6 damage to each creature whose space the swarm occupies at the end of its move. There is no attack roll or miss chance from cover or concealment.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Distraction (Ex). A living creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space must make a DC 11 Fortitude save or be nauseated for 1 round. The general subtype limits this to creatures vulnerable to the swarm’s damage. A nauseated creature can take only one move action per turn. Casting or concentrating on spells in the swarm requires a Concentration check at DC 20 + spell level. Skills demanding concentration require a DC 20 Concentration check.
Wounding (Ex). A living creature damaged by the swarm then loses 1 HP per round from bleeding. Additional wounds do not increase the rate. A DC 10 Heal check, a cure spell, or other healing magic stops it.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Blindsense (Ex). Locate creatures within 20 ft. Total concealment still applies unless the swarm can actually see them. Swarm damage ignores concealment.
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light.
Swarm traits. One pool of HP and one set of saves. Occupy a shared, shapeable 10-ft. space and fit through gaps large enough for one bat. Entering or moving through a hostile space provokes as normal. The swarm never threatens or makes opportunity attacks. It cannot grapple and is unaffected by grappling, trips, bull rushes, critical hits, or flanking. Effects aimed at a fixed number of creatures do not affect it, subject to the hive-mind exception for mind-affecting effects. Area effects deal 50% more damage. At 0 HP it disperses. It does not become staggered or dying. If rendered unconscious by nonlethal damage, it disperses until HP exceed that damage. Resolve strong wind against Diminutive size.
Weapon damage. Use weapon damage immunity under the shared subtype rule, supported by the 2006 Monster Manual errata. The SRD entry still has the earlier half-damage line.
Shared swarm vulnerabilities. A lit torch used as an improvised weapon deals 1d3 fire damage on a hit. A thrown lit lantern deals 1d4 fire damage to creatures in adjacent squares where it breaks. Energy damage from a weapon can still apply if the weapon’s ordinary damage does not.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Listen +11, Spot +11. Each includes a +4 racial bonus that is lost if blindsense is negated.
Feats: Alertness, Lightning Reflexes.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Temperate deserts. Solitary, flight of 2–4 swarms, or colony of 11–20 swarms. No treasure or advancement. Level adjustment —. Nocturnal and never found aboveground in daylight. It tries to surround warm-blooded prey.

gm.title: Printing conflicts
lines:
Armor Class. The table prints touch 14 and flat-footed 12. Its listed +4 size and +2 Dexterity would give touch 16 and flat-footed 14 using the standard AC rules.
Weapon damage. The Bat Swarm table lists half damage from slashing and piercing. The shared Diminutive Swarm subtype grants immunity to all weapon damage, confirmed for the Bat Swarm in the 17 February 2006 Monster Manual v3.5 errata. Use immunity at the table.

lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Defenses and Legacy
lines: Adult batracines have Leap. The p. 8 monster rules allow an instantaneous jump forward or straight upward 20 ft. plus 1 ft. per Hit Die, capped at 35 ft. A 2-HD batracine can jump 22 ft. It uses this to take birds or reach water when threatened. The creature never becomes Afflicted and needs no cinnabryl. It is immune to the amber lotus’s sleep effect. The compendium’s general monster Legacy rules allow three uses per day once fully active and immediate use once activated. The initial week permits one use per day. Its powers fade after leaving the Red Curse and Haze. See printed pp. 6–9.

gm.title: Parasites
lines: Cardinal ticks can infest this creature. If the specimen is infested, a melee encounter leaves the combatants with 5% infestation. Infestation increases by 15 percentage points each time its host attempts to use a Legacy, up to 50% in nonhumanoids. A cinnabryl ointment clears it. Scratching costs 1 HP per percentage point removed unless the special Jibarú medicine is used. See Parasite, printed p. 85.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Common river carnivore, active at dusk and dawn. Family organization and 1d4 appearing. Adults usually den alone near the Dream River and pair in mating season, with 2–4 pups. They gather to hunt when food is short. They take forest animals and favor birds. Fish and amphibians are outside their diet. Pups sell for 5 gp and a trained pet for 20 gp. The book describes their blood as an ingredient in a potion to counter magical sleep.

lines:
Adept Climber (black or spectacled bear). Gain a 25-ft. climb speed.
Arctic Traveler (polar bear). Gain advantage on saves to avoid Exhaustion. Tolerate temperatures down to −50°F and ignore difficult terrain from ice or snow.
Fearsome Growl (any bear, 1/day). As a bonus action, growl. Each creature within 15 ft. that hears it makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Frightened of the bear until the end of the bear’s next turn. On a success, it is immune to Fearsome Growl from all bears for 24 hours.
Clever Claws (sloth bear). Use claws in place of thieves’ tools to open locks, with +3 to the relevant Dexterity check.
Powerful Jaws (giant panda or sun bear). Bite deals an extra 4 (1d8) damage and deals maximum damage to Plants. A bear with this trait cannot use Multiattack.
Sprint (black, brown, polar, spectacled, or sun bear, recharges after a short or long rest). When the bear moves on its turn during combat, it can triple its speed until the turn ends.

gm.title: Primal Companion
lines: This optional Beast Master feature is available at ranger level 3 and replaces Ranger’s Companion. The beast is friendly and uses the Land, Sea, or Sky stat block. Choose an animal appropriate for that profile. Whatever its shape, it has primal markings. It acts during the ranger’s turn and may move or react on its own. Unless the ranger commands it using a bonus action, its default action is Dodge. The ranger may instead give up one attack when taking the Attack action to command the beast to Attack. If the ranger is incapacitated, the beast can choose its action freely. Within an hour after the beast dies, the ranger may touch it as an action and spend a spell slot of level 1 or higher. After one minute it returns to life at full HP. After a long rest the ranger may instead summon another beast into an unoccupied space within 5 feet, choosing the profile and animal shape anew. An existing companion vanishes when the replacement appears. The beast also vanishes if the ranger dies.

gm.title: Scaling
lines: Natural armor gives AC 13 + the ranger’s proficiency bonus. The beast uses that proficiency bonus, understands the languages its ranger speaks, and has darkvision 60 ft. and passive Perception 12. The printed challenge line has no rating. Medium Beast. HP equals 5 + 5 × ranger level, with one d8 Hit Die per ranger level. Walk and climb 40 ft. each. STR 14, DEX 14, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 14, CHA 11.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Primal Bond lets the ranger add their proficiency bonus to the beast’s ability checks and saving throws. Charge adds 1d6 slashing damage if the beast moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with Maul that turn. A creature hit this way makes a Strength save against the ranger’s spell save DC or falls prone.

gm.title: Action
lines: Maul is a melee weapon attack against one target within 5 ft. Use the ranger’s spell attack modifier to hit. On a hit, deal 1d8 + 2 + PB slashing damage.

gm.title: Primal Companion
lines: At Ranger level 3, choose a Land, Sea, or Sky form and an animal suited to it. The beast has visible primal markings, is Friendly to you and your allies, and obeys you. It vanishes if you die. It acts on your turn, and it can move and use its reaction independently. It normally takes Dodge. Spend a bonus action to have it take another action, or replace one attack of your Attack action to have it use Beast’s Strike. If you are Incapacitated, the beast chooses its own actions. If it died within the past hour, take a Magic action to touch it and spend a spell slot. It revives after 1 minute with full HP. Finishing a long rest lets you choose a new form and appearance, summoning it into an unoccupied space within 5 ft. and replacing the prior beast.

gm.title: Scaling
lines: AC is 13 + the ranger’s Wisdom modifier. The beast uses the ranger’s proficiency bonus. It has no CR and grants 0 XP. It understands the ranger’s languages. Passive Perception 12. HP is 5 + five times the ranger level. The beast has one d8 Hit Die per ranger level.

gm.title: Statistics

gm.title: Traits
lines: Primal Bond. Add the ranger’s proficiency bonus to all of the beast’s ability checks and saving throws.

Choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing on summoning. If the beast moved 20 ft. or more in a straight line toward the target before hitting, add 1d6 of that type. A Large or smaller creature hit under that movement condition also falls Prone.

gm.title: Higher-level Beast Master features
lines: At Ranger level 7, whenever a bonus action commands the beast to act, you may also have it use its own bonus action for Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help. Its attack damage can be Force or its normal type. At level 11, a command to use Beast’s Strike lets it strike twice. The first time each turn it hits a creature affected by your Hunter’s Mark, it deals extra Force damage equal to the mark’s bonus damage. At level 15, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, it can also affect your beast if it is within 30 ft.

gm.title: Summon Beast
lines: Summon Beast is a level 2 Conjuration spell for druids and rangers. Cast it as an action, at 90-ft. range, with verbal, somatic, and material components. The materials are a feather, tuft of fur, and fish tail inside a gilded acorn worth at least 200 GP. Concentration lasts up to 1 hour. Choose Air, Land, or Water and a native animal appearance. The spirit appears in an unoccupied space you can see within range, and it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends.

gm.title: Initiative and commands
lines: The spirit allies with you and your allies. It takes its turn immediately after yours at the same initiative count and obeys your verbal commands without an action cost. If you give no orders, it takes Dodge and uses its movement to avoid danger.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Small neutral Beast. Str 18, Dex 11, Con 16, Int 4, Wis 14, Cha 5. Base save modifiers in that order are +4, +0, +3, −3, +2 and −3. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12. Understands the caster’s languages. No CR, 0 XP, and proficiency bonus equals the caster’s.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. Make a number of Rend attacks equal to half the slot level, rounded down. Rend. Make a melee attack roll using the caster’s spell attack modifier with a 5-ft. reach. A hit deals 1d8 + 4 + the slot level in Piercing damage.

gm.title: Scaling
lines: AC is 11 + the spell slot level. Start with 30 HP and add 5 HP per slot level above 2.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Pack Tactics. The spirit rolls attacks against a creature with advantage if at least one spirit ally within 5 ft. of that creature is free of the Incapacitated condition.
Water Breathing. The spirit breathes only underwater.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: The caster chooses a native water animal. The portrait shows a crocodile.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: Bhaal's huge, spined Beast avatar has a biting maw, claws, and a spiked carapace.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Str +16, Dex +14, Cha +9. Skills Athletics +16, Perception +10, Stealth +14. Resists necrotic. Immune to acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Immune to charmed, exhaustion, frightened, incapacitated, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, stunned, and unconscious. Darkvision 120 ft., truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 20. Abyssal, Common, Primordial, and Undercommon.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Minsc and Boo's Journal of Villainy, chapter 3, Campaign Villains, p. 95.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Avatar of Bhaal. At 0 HP, the form breaks apart. The Slayer returns within 24 hours, 2d6 miles from the place the Ravager fell. Cull the Weak. After Ravager melee damage leaves a creature at 20 HP or less, it must pass a DC 21 Constitution save or fall to 0 HP. Immutable Form. Effects cannot change its form. Legendary Resistance, three per day. The Ravager can turn a failed save into a success. Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against magic. Magic Weapons. Claw, Bite, and Spines are magical attacks. Spiked Hide. At the start of the Ravager’s turn, any creature grappling it or in its grip takes 16 (3d10) piercing damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. Use the referenced Fear aura if available, then make one Bite and two Claws, or make two Spines attacks. Claw. +16 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 22 (3d8 + 9) slashing plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. Bite. +16 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deals 25 (3d10 + 9) piercing plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. A Large or smaller creature damaged by Bite is grappled, escape DC 20. While the grapple remains, the Ravager has no other Bite attack. When either hit damages a creature, it makes a DC 21 Constitution save. Failure subtracts the damage taken from its HP maximum until Greater Restoration or comparable magic removes the reduction. It dies if that maximum falls to 0. Spines. +14 to hit at 60/120 ft., one target. Deals 17 (3d6 + 7) piercing damage. A failed DC 19 Constitution save stuns the target through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The Ravager has three legendary actions. It can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn and regains spent actions when its own turn starts. Detect. Make a Wisdom (Perception) check. Smash. Creatures in a 10-ft. cube originating from the Ravager make DC 20 Constitution saves. Failure deals 36 (8d8) thunder damage and pushes a target 5 ft. Success halves the damage and prevents the push. The sound carries 100 ft. Spiky Carapace, costs two actions. The Ravager extends its spines. A creature that starts its turn within 5 ft. makes a DC 21 Dexterity save or takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage, half on a success.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The 2021 Multiattack refers to a Fear aura with no rules in the block. Spiky Carapace has no stated end time. The separate Slayer avatar on p. 93 is Humanoid.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Athletics +4, Perception +5. Passive Perception 15. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exceptional Vision. Add +10 to Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
High-Speed Dive (recharges after a short or long rest). After descending at least 30 ft. on its turn, the bird can Dash as a bonus action. If it does, it has advantage on its next attack that turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d4 + 3) slashing damage. The bird grapples a Tiny creature it hits (escape DC 12). It instead attaches to a Small or larger creature it hits. While attached, the bird can attack only that creature and has advantage on Beak attacks against it. The creature or someone within reach of it can spend an action to roll DC 12 Strength (Athletics). The attached creature takes 2 (1d4) slashing damage whether the check succeeds or fails. A success detaches the bird. The bird can detach by spending 5 ft. of movement.

gm.title: Optional Bird Features
lines:
Crushing Grip (eagle or falcon). As an action, choose a creature the bird is grappling or attached to. The target makes a DC 13 Strength save against 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage, taking half on a success.
Aerial Pursuit (merlin, replaces High-Speed Dive, recharges after a short or long rest). When the bird starts its turn airborne, it can triple its flying speed for that turn. If it descends at least 30 ft., it has advantage on its next attack that turn.
Agile Flyer (kite, harrier, or hawk). While airborne, add +5 to Dexterity saves and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
Decapitating Strike (eagle or owl). A critical hit against a Tiny target removes its head. The target dies if it needs that head to survive.
Glide (condor or golden eagle). The bird can finish a short rest while flying horizontally.
Night Hunter (owl or letter-winged kite). Gain darkvision 120 ft. and +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Ocean Hunter (osprey). If the bird starts its turn above water, underwater combat imposes no disadvantage on its attacks until that turn ends.
Powerful Impact (falcon, raises CR from 1/2 to 1). Descending at least 20 ft. immediately before hitting with Talons or Rending Talons on that turn adds 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage.
Scavenger’s Resilience (vulture or caracara). Gain advantage on Constitution saves and resistance to poison damage.
Wind Hover (kestrel or osprey). The bird can hover.

gm.title: Description
lines: A war dog marked by a divine bloodline. A blooded handler can send it after a missing heir or a rival scion.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Medium beast. Neutral. Vos hounds are neutral evil.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare in Cerilia, principally Anuire. Solitary, or pack for Vos hounds. Appearing 1d4, or 3d6 Vos hounds. Active any time. Omnivore. Semi-intelligence 2–4. Medium, 4–6 ft. long. Morale 11–12 or 20. No treasure or magic resistance. Perception slight, Seeming none.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. One attack for 2d4 damage. A Vos hound instead bites for 2d6. A trained hound generally pins the quarry first. It attacks if attacked, ordered to bite, or convinced its handler is threatened.

gm.title: Tracking scions
lines: Automatically detect a blooded trail within 1 mile or one left in the area in the last five days if rain has not cleared it. At up to 5 miles, or for a blooded trail in that radius from the last two days, use 50%. Add 15 percentage points for a matching bloodline derivation, 15 for a named target whose personal effect the hound can scent, and 10 for a target with a great bloodline. When seeking any scion, exclude the hunting party and prefer a matching derivation in the area over a nearer nonmatching one. The chance to find a specified unblooded person within 1 mile is 50%.

gm.title: Handler bond
lines: Only a blooded handler can bond with the hound. A breeder’s imprinting ritual binds it for life unless its handler mistreats it, dies, or transfers the bond by ritual. With a handler of the same bloodline derivation, its combat morale is 20. If it believes that handler is in danger, it fights to the death unless called off by them.

gm.title: Bloodline and Seeming
lines: Tainted bloodline 1d3, with a Bloodmark. There is a 5% chance of one extra minor blood ability appropriate to the derivation. Choose from Courage, Detect Illusion, Detect Life, Direction Sense, Iron Will, Long Life, Poison Sense, or Resistance. Slight Perception only warns it that something is wrong with a creature disguised by the Seeming. It cannot determine what the disguise hides.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The page 14 combat prose gives the ordinary bite as 2d4 + 1. The stat table on p. 15 gives 2d4. Use 2d4 as the table default.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Two claws +11 melee each, 1d8 + 8 each. Bite +6 melee, 2d6 + 4.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Improved Grab (Ex). After a claw hit on a Medium or smaller foe, attempt a grapple at +16 as a free action without a touch attack or attack of opportunity. A hold pulls the foe into the attacker’s space without provoking. Use the ordinary grapple or hold only with the striking limb or mouth at −20 on grapple checks. In the latter case the animal keeps its Dexterity bonus to AC, still threatens, and may use its remaining attacks against other foes. The first hold adds no damage by itself. A successful grapple check in later rounds automatically deals the damage of the attack used to grab. The animal can move with the foe if it can drag its weight. The foe escapes by winning an opposed grapple check in place of an attack, or by using Escape Artist as a standard action against the grapple check.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, sees twice as far as a human and keeps color and detail.
Scent. Detect ordinary creatures within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Double those distances for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action identifies the direction, and within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.
Track by scent. Take the Track feat’s usual checks, with DC 10 for a typical fresh trail and +2 DC per hour since it was left. Surface conditions and poor visibility do not affect scent tracking. Odor strength and number of creatures can shift the DC.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Listen +4, Spot +7, Swim +12. Feats. Endurance, Run, Track.
Swim checks have a +4 racial bonus, included in Swim +12.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines:
Cold forests. Solitary or pair. Always neutral, no treasure. Advancement 7–10 HD (Large). No level adjustment.
A territorial bear can fight with its claws before securing a hold. The SRD suggests this block for other large bears, including grizzlies.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Bite. One attack for 1d4 damage. Each bite causes 1 HP of bleeding per round until direct pressure is applied. Keep the pressure in place until the wound has been bandaged for more than 24 hours. The bite also has a printed 20% chance of vermilia infection.

gm.title: Vermilia
lines: The separate Parasite entry says living targets save vs. poison to avoid infection. Undead contract it automatically, then can save vs. death magic each day at day’s end to avoid that day’s damage. That save carries a penalty equal to the day’s vermilia damage. A Legacy user takes an additional −1 per Legacy on vermilia saves. Damage doubles daily from 1 HP on day one until cure disease, heal, or the setting’s special remedy treats it. It counts as a +2 magical weapon for purposes of affecting undead or other magical creatures. The text does not explicitly specify how the bite’s 20% check interacts with the general save. See printed pp. 85–86.

gm.title: Parasites
lines: Cardinal ticks can infest this creature. If the specimen is infested, a melee encounter leaves the combatants with 5% infestation. Infestation increases by 15 percentage points each time its host attempts to use a Legacy, up to 50% in nonhumanoids. A cinnabryl ointment clears it. Scratching costs 1 HP per percentage point removed unless the special Jibarú medicine is used. See Parasite, printed p. 85.

lines: Uncommon temperate forest and mountain carnivore, active at dusk and dawn. Family organization and 1d4 appearing. It usually flees unless feeding or protecting pups, bites, then springs away. Mates stay together for life and typically raise 4–6 pups in a burrow. It hunts rodents, chiefly voats, and often shelters near rock ledges or roots. An undamaged treated pelt is worth up to 5 gp. Inheritors protect the animals because they can find cinnabryl.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claw. Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage. If the target is a Small or larger creature, the clawfish can enter its space and attach to it.
While attached, the clawfish follows the target without provoking opportunity attacks and cannot use Claw. A creature that can reach it can use an action to detach it with a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On success it moves to an unoccupied space of its choice within 5 ft. of the target. It also detaches by spending 5 ft. of movement or if it becomes Grappled, Incapacitated, Prone, or Restrained.
Electrocute (Recharge 6). Every creature touching the clawfish takes 7 (2d6) lightning damage. If the clawfish is immersed, every other creature within 10 ft. touching the same body of water makes a DC 11 Dexterity save or takes 7 (2d6) lightning damage.

gm.title: Angulotl training

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Overwhelming Attack (2 Ferocity). Make a Bite. A hit deals extra lightning damage equal to PB, and the target loses reactions until the start of the clawfish’s next turn.
Level 3, Coiling Claws (5 Ferocity). Make a Bite against a Medium or smaller creature. A hit also leaves the target Grappled with escape DC 10 + PB. The target stays Restrained during this grapple and the clawfish cannot make a signature attack against another target.
Level 5, Lightning Bomb (8 Ferocity). Every creature within 10 ft. makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB, taking PBd8 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Lightning Retaliation (short or long rest). When a creature the clawfish sees within 5 ft. attacks it or its caregiver, the clawfish can shock the attacker. The attacker makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB, taking PBd6 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Riverkith. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and the Mystic Connection feature gains a swim speed equal to walking speed and can hold their breath for 15 minutes. Once per long rest, they can use a bonus action to breathe lightning in a 30-ft. cone. Every creature in it makes a Dexterity save against the Beastheart’s exploit save DC, taking 6d6 lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Attack
lines: Bite +6 melee (1d8 + 6) or tail slap +6 melee (1d12 + 6).

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Bite +6 melee (1d8 + 6) or tail slap +6 melee (1d12 + 6).

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Improved Grab (Ex). After a bite hits, the crocodile can attempt a grapple as a free action. It needs no touch attack and provokes no attack of opportunity. The default size limit is at least one category smaller, so Small or smaller. If the crocodile wins, it holds the target in its jaws, drags it into deep water and tries to pin it on the bottom. The crocodile can pull a held target into its space and move with it if it can drag the target, without provoking for the pull. The initial hold adds no damage. Later successful grapple checks deal bite damage. It can hold with its jaws alone at −20 on grapple checks. With that option it can keep its Dexterity bonus to AC, threaten normally and use any remaining attacks on other foes.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines: Hold Breath (Ex). It can hold its breath for 68 rounds (4 × Constitution 17) before risking drowning. Low-light vision doubles normal human sight distance in dim light and retains color and detail.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide +7, Listen +4, Spot +4, Swim +12. Alertness, Skill Focus (Hide). It gains a +4 racial Hide bonus in water and a +10 cover bonus while only its eyes and nostrils are exposed. The +8 racial Swim bonus applies to special maneuvers and hazards. The animal can take 10 even under threat and can run while swimming in a straight line.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Ambushes prey while mostly submerged in a warm river or marsh. Encounter one or a colony of 6–11. Advancement 4–5 HD (Medium). No treasure or listed level adjustment.

gm.title: Full attack

gm.title: Special attacks

gm.title: Special qualities
lines: Low-light vision doubles normal human sight distance in dim light and retains color and detail. Scent (Ex). Detects opponents at 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double these ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction. Within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.

Poor visibility and the surface do not hinder scent tracking.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: It stalks from cover and uses its speed to pounce. Packs hunt together. Encounter one, a pair, or a pack of 3–6. Advancement 5–8 HD (Large). No treasure or listed level adjustment.

gm.title: Print distinction
lines: This SRD archive uses Large size, 10-ft. space, and 2d6 + 4 talons. Wizards’ February 2006 Monster Manual errata uses Medium size, 5-ft. space, and 1d8 + 4 talons in its replacement table.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A single-humped camel with wide padded feet and a rolling gait.

gm.title: Special attacks mechanics
lines: Spitting · An ill-tempered camel has a 50% chance to spit at someone who tries to ride it or use it as a pack animal. The victim then has a 25% chance of being blinded for 1–3 rounds.

Herd stampede · A frightened herd has a 25% chance of stampeding. Roll 2d4 camels for each creature in its path that fails to take cover. Each camel deals 1–4 damage to that creature. Trampled creatures stay down until the herd passes.

gm.title: Handling mechanics
lines: Carrying capacity · Load by weight in gold pieces: 250 normal, 400 encumbered, 520 fully encumbered. Camels kneel to be loaded and often refuse to rise with more than their encumbered load.
Desert camel use · A steady mount and pack animal that carries heavy loads across difficult terrain.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: 1–12 appearing. Steady (12) morale. Animal to semi-intelligent (1–4).
Common, diurnal herd herbivore. The table lists any land for terrain and Nil for alignment, treasure, special defenses, and magic resistance.
TSR, Monstrous Compendium Al-Qadim Appendix (1992), unnumbered Camel leaf (p. 11).

gm.title: Feather of Diatryma Summoning
lines: The rare feather requires attunement. Use an action to speak the command word and toss the feather into a Large unoccupied space on the ground within 5 ft. The bird appears for up to 6 hours. It reverts sooner at 0 HP or if the user touches it and spends an action to repeat the command word. The feather can summon again after 7 days have elapsed from the reversion. The summoned bird is friendly to the user and their companions and can be ridden. It understands the user’s languages and follows spoken commands. In the absence of orders, it defends itself and takes no other actions.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A low-slung, armored dinosaur with a spiked back and a heavy tail club.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. STR +4, DEX +0, CON +2, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -3. Perception 11. Stealth 10. Senses —. Languages —.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Nosolorol, Cubil de Monstruos (licensed Spanish edition of Kobold Press’s Monster Vault), pp. 108–109, “Anquilosaurio”.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Hardy. Treat any critical hit against the dinosaur as a normal hit.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tail attacks.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. The hit deals 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must pass a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
Tail Sweep (Recharge 4–6). Every creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 27 (6d8) bludgeoning damage, is pushed up to 15 ft. away and falls prone. A successful save halves the damage and prevents the push and prone effects. After use, roll a d6 at the start of each ankylosaurus turn. A 4–6 restores the action. A short or long rest also restores it.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Defensive Huddle. When a creature the ankylosaurus can see hits it with a weapon attack, the ankylosaurus turns its armored back into the blow and halves the damage it takes from the attack.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. STR +4, DEX +2, CON +3, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -3. Perception 13. Stealth 14. Senses —. Languages —.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Hardy. Treat any critical hit against the dinosaur as a normal hit.
Hold Breath. The plesiosaurus can hold its breath for 1 hour.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Flipper Slam. While underwater, the plesiosaurus sends a shock wave through the water in a 15-ft. cone. Each creature in the cone must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or be off-balance until the end of its next turn. While off-balance, the creature has half speed and disadvantage on its first attack roll on each of its turns.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A stocky gray-brown dinosaur with three facial horns and a broad neck frill.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. STR +6, DEX -1, CON +3, INT -4, WIS +0, CHA -3. Perception 10. Stealth 9. Senses —. Languages —.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Hardy. Treat any critical hit against the dinosaur as a normal hit.
Trampling Charge. If the triceratops moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and then hits it with Gore on the same turn, the target must pass a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the triceratops can make a Stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Gore attacks.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) piercing damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. A hit deals 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Warning Bugle. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone must pass a DC 14 Wisdom save or be frightened until the end of its next turn. If the triceratops uses Warning Bugle before the 20 ft. of movement for Trampling Charge, its charge target has disadvantage on this Wisdom save. If that target fails the charge’s Strength save, the triceratops can Stomp the prone target without spending a bonus action.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Traits
lines: Hardy. Treat any critical hit against the dinosaur as a normal hit.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Tail attack against different targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 31 (4d12 + 5) piercing damage. A Large or smaller target is automatically grappled and remains restrained until the grapple ends. The target can use its action to try to escape (DC 16). While the grapple lasts, the tyrannosaurus cannot Bite another target.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 23 (4d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Rending Shake. One creature grappled by the tyrannosaurus must pass a DC 16 Strength save or take 6 (1d12) slashing damage, be thrown up to 20 ft. in a random direction and fall prone. If the thrown target strikes a solid surface, it takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 ft. it was thrown. If it is thrown at another creature, that other creature must pass a DC 16 Dexterity save or take the same bludgeoning damage and fall prone.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit this way becomes grappled, escape DC 12. It is restrained for the duration of the grapple. The velociraptor cannot Bite another target while this grapple lasts.

Maul. A creature the velociraptor is grappling makes a DC 12 Strength save. It takes 10 (4d4) slashing damage on failure or half on success.

Double those ranges for strong odors, triple for overpowering ones. Use a move action to learn the direction and approach within 5 ft. to pinpoint.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Two claws, each +4 melee for 1d4+2, and one bite, −1 melee for 1d6+1.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, see twice as far as a human with color and detail intact.
Scent (Ex). Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double that range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering odors. A move action determines direction. Within 5 ft., locate the source exactly. Track and scent allow tracking by smell with a Wisdom or Survival check. A fresh trail typically starts at DC 10. Add 2 per hour the trail is cold and adjust for quarry count and odor. Surface conditions and poor visibility do not alter this scent check.

gm.title: Skills and feats

It cannot end the rage voluntarily. It can burrow through material softer than solid rock. Except in very loose material, it generally leaves a usable tunnel 5 ft. in diameter.

lines: A massive brown bat with long ears, spread dark membrane wings, and hooked feet.

Hide +4, Listen +12, Move Silently +11, Spot +8. The +4 racial bonuses to Listen and Spot are lost if blindsense is negated.
Feats: Alertness, Stealthy.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An enormous thickset brown bear with dark shaggy shoulders, heavy hooked claws and a broad muzzle.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Touch AC 10, flat-footed AC 16. AC modifiers −1 size, +1 Dex, and +7 natural. Base attack +9, grapple +23. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +12, Ref +9, Will +9.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersDi-Do.rtf, DIRE BEAR. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/direBear.htm

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Two claws +19 melee each, 2d4 + 10 each, and bite +13 melee, 2d8 + 5.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Improved Grab (Ex). After hitting with a claw, the bear deals its normal claw damage and can start a grapple as a free action without a touch attack or an attack of opportunity. By the general Improved Grab rule it works on Medium or smaller opponents. A successful hold pulls the opponent into the bear’s space without provoking. After the initial hold, a successful grapple check in a later round deals the establishing claw’s damage.

gm.title: Improved Grab at the table
lines: Grapple normally at +23, or hold using only the claw at −20 to grapple checks. In the latter case the bear can threaten and use its other attacks, retains its Dexterity bonus to AC, and is free of the grapple condition itself. It can move with the held creature if it can drag the weight. The held creature can try to escape by beating the bear’s opposed grapple check, or substitute Escape Artist as a standard action.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light, with color and detail.
Scent. Detect by smell out to 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind or 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action gives the direction. Pinpoint the source within 5 ft.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Listen +10, Spot +10, Swim +13. Feats are Alertness, Endurance, Run, Toughness, and Weapon Focus (claw).

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Cold forests. Solitary or pair. A dire bear can reach 12 ft. long and weigh 8,000 lb. It usually ignores creatures that steer clear and defends a kill or other food. Advancement 13–16 HD (Large) or 17–36 HD (Huge). No level adjustment or treasure.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A massive tawny brown bear with a heavy shoulder hump, broad paws and small ivory projections along its upper back.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Level 11 Elite Brute. Initiative +8. Fortitude 25, Reflex 22, Will 23. Bloodied 138. Perception +9. Saving throws +2. 1 action point. No listed languages.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, King of the Trollhaunt Warrens, first printing, October 2008, Adventure Book Two, Encounter W4, Mound of Skulls, stat block p. 17 and encounter pp. 16–17.

gm.title: Printed powers
lines:
Claw. Melee basic attack, standard, at-will. Reach 2. +15 vs. AC. Hit for 2d8 + 6 damage.
Maul. Melee, standard, at-will. Make two Claw attacks. If both hit the same target, make a secondary attack against it at +13 vs. AC. A hit grabs the target until escape.
Ursine Crush. Melee, standard, at-will. Deal 4d8 + 6 damage to a grabbed creature without an attack roll.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: Norgg’s bear lies below the ledge and gnaws on bones. In combat it attacks the closest target, using Maul to establish a grab before Ursine Crush. Norgg and the bear stay in the chamber if the party flees.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Athletics +5, Perception +5. Passive Perception 15. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exceptional Vision. Add +10 to Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
High-Speed Dive (recharges after a short or long rest). After descending at least 30 ft. on its turn, the bird can Dash as a bonus action. If it does, it has advantage on its next attack that turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Heavy Beak or Rending Talons for each.
Heavy Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. A critical hit leaves the target Dazed until the start of the bird’s next turn.
Rending Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage. The bird grapples a Medium or smaller creature it hits (escape DC 13). While grappling, the bird can attack only that target and has advantage on Heavy Beak attacks against it. The target takes 4 (1d8) slashing damage each time it makes a check to end the grapple.
Crushing Grip. One target the bird is grappling makes a DC 13 Strength save against 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage. It takes half on a success. Failure by 5 or more also leaves the target Dazed until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: A Dazed creature can do one of the following on its turn: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. If it becomes Dazed during its turn, the turn ends. Extra actions granted by effects such as Haste or Action Surge remain available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration remove the condition. The GM can allow other remedies.

gm.title: Optional Bird Features
lines:
Alternate Crushing Grip (eagle or falcon). If you choose this version, use it in place of the built-in Crushing Grip. As an action, choose a creature the bird is grappling or attached to. The target makes a DC 13 Strength save against 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage, taking half on a success.
Aerial Pursuit (merlin, replaces High-Speed Dive, recharges after a short or long rest). When the bird starts its turn airborne, it can triple its flying speed for that turn. If it descends at least 30 ft., it has advantage on its next attack that turn.
Agile Flyer (kite, harrier, or hawk). While airborne, add +5 to Dexterity saves and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
Decapitating Strike (eagle or owl). A critical hit against a Tiny target removes its head. The target dies if it needs that head to survive.
Glide (condor or golden eagle). The bird can finish a short rest while flying horizontally.
Night Hunter (owl or letter-winged kite). Gain darkvision 120 ft. and +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Ocean Hunter (osprey). If the bird starts its turn above water, underwater combat imposes no disadvantage on its attacks until that turn ends.
Powerful Impact (falcon, +1 CR). Descending at least 20 ft. immediately before hitting with Talons or Rending Talons on that turn adds 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage.
Scavenger’s Resilience (vulture or caracara). Gain advantage on Constitution saves and resistance to poison damage.
Wind Hover (kestrel or osprey). The bird can hover.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Athletics +5, Perception +5. Passive Perception 15. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exceptional Vision. Add +10 to Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attack.
High-Speed Dive (recharges after a short or long rest). After descending at least 30 ft. on its turn, the bird can Dash as a bonus action. If it does, it has advantage on its next attack that turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Heavy Beak or Rending Talons for each.
Heavy Beak. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. A critical hit leaves the target Dazed until the start of the bird’s next turn.
Rending Talons. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage. The bird grapples a Medium or smaller creature it hits (escape DC 13). While grappling, the bird can attack only that target and has advantage on Heavy Beak attacks against it. The target takes 4 (1d8) slashing damage each time it makes a check to end the grapple.
Crushing Grip. One target the bird is grappling makes a DC 13 Strength save against 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage. It takes half on a success. Failure by 5 or more also leaves the target Dazed until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: A Dazed creature can do one of the following on its turn: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. If it becomes Dazed during its turn, the turn ends. Extra actions granted by effects such as Haste or Action Surge remain available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration remove the condition. The GM can allow other remedies.

gm.title: Optional Bird Features
lines:
Alternate Crushing Grip (eagle or falcon). If you choose this version, use it in place of the built-in Crushing Grip. As an action, choose a creature the bird is grappling or attached to. The target makes a DC 13 Strength save against 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage, taking half on a success.
Aerial Pursuit (merlin, replaces High-Speed Dive, recharges after a short or long rest). When the bird starts its turn airborne, it can triple its flying speed for that turn. If it descends at least 30 ft., it has advantage on its next attack that turn.
Agile Flyer (kite, harrier, or hawk). While airborne, add +5 to Dexterity saves and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
Decapitating Strike (eagle or owl). A critical hit against a Tiny target removes its head. The target dies if it needs that head to survive.
Glide (condor or golden eagle). The bird can finish a short rest while flying horizontally.
Night Hunter (owl or letter-winged kite). Gain darkvision 120 ft. and +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Ocean Hunter (osprey). If the bird starts its turn above water, underwater combat imposes no disadvantage on its attacks until that turn ends.
Powerful Impact (falcon, +1 CR). Descending at least 20 ft. immediately before hitting with Talons or Rending Talons on that turn adds 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage.
Scavenger’s Resilience (vulture or caracara). Gain advantage on Constitution saves and resistance to poison damage.
Wind Hover (kestrel or osprey). The bird can hover.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Improved Grab (Ex). After a bite hit on a Medium or smaller foe, attempt a grapple at +17 as a free action without a touch attack or attack of opportunity. A hold pulls the foe into the attacker’s space without provoking. Use the ordinary grapple or hold only with the striking limb or mouth at −20 on grapple checks. In the latter case the animal keeps its Dexterity bonus to AC, still threatens, and may use its remaining attacks against other foes. The first hold adds no damage by itself. A successful grapple check in later rounds automatically deals the damage of the attack used to grab. The animal can move with the foe if it can drag its weight. The foe escapes by winning an opposed grapple check in place of an attack, or by using Escape Artist as a standard action against the grapple check.
Pounce (Ex). A charge ends in the full attack plus two rakes. Follow the normal movement restrictions and AC penalty for charging.
Rake (Ex). Two additional rear-claw attacks against a grappled target, each +12 melee for 1d6 + 3, without the ordinary −4 natural-attack penalty in a grapple. The shared rake rule calls for starting the turn already grappling. Pounce explicitly adds two rakes to the charge.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:

The description mentions leaping at larger prey. The Improved Grab rule still uses the normal size limit because the entry gives no explicit size exception.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A translucent eyeless sea worm about 12 ft. long and 2 ft. thick, with a flattened tail and a suction-cup mouth containing three rows of crystalline fangs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Descending AC 4 (10). THAC0 15. One attack per round. Average morale (8–10). Animal intelligence (1). No magic resistance. Size L, 12 ft. long. No treasure.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: TSR 2524, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix, printed p. 26.

gm.title: Attacks
lines:
Suction bite. One attack for 2d4 damage. It detects movement and strikes from behind or below. On a hit, it attaches and deals its damage again automatically each round until the victim succeeds on a bend bars roll to detach it.
Swallow Whole. On a natural attack roll of 18–20 it swallows a man-sized or smaller target. The book supplies no separate save, swallowed damage, or escape procedure.

gm.title: School tactics
lines: Only one worm attacks at a time. Once the active worm loses half of its HP, it disengages and another takes its turn. The rotation continues until all are injured, then those still able to swim try to escape.

gm.title: Defenses and Legacy
lines: It is almost invisible underwater because of its translucent body and is immune to amber lotus. No detection modifier is given. It rarely gains a Legacy and is immune to Affliction, so it needs no cinnabryl. XP is 2,000 for a specimen with a Legacy. The compendium’s general monster Legacy rules allow three uses per day once fully active and immediate use once activated. The initial week permits one use per day. Its powers fade after leaving the Red Curse and Haze. See printed pp. 6–9.

gm.title: Print ambiguity
lines: The entry prints descending AC 4 (10) and does not give the condition for switching to 10.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Uncommon aquatic carnivore, active at any time. School organization and 1d6+6 appearing. Echyans breed in coastal rivers, with spring hatchlings heading to sea. Adults follow fish in summer and return to the rivers in winter. They sometimes come ashore for tortle eggs, and worms caught in daylight bury themselves partly in sand.

lines: Choose slam +16 melee (2d6 + 10) and two stamps +11 melee each (2d6 + 5 each), or one gore +16 melee (2d8 + 15).

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Trample (Ex). Spend a full-round action to move up to 80 ft. and pass completely over the spaces of Large or smaller opponents. Each affected opponent takes 2d8 + 15 bludgeoning damage at most once that round. It can make an attack of opportunity at −4, or forgo that attack and make a DC 25 Reflex save for half damage. Passing over only part of a creature’s space allows the attack of opportunity at −4 and does not trample it. If the elephant ends in an illegal space, move it back to its last legal space or to a closer legal space if available. The DC is Strength-based.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, sees twice as far as a human and keeps color and detail.
Scent. Detect ordinary creatures within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Double those distances for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action identifies the direction, and within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.

gm.title: Skills and feats

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines:
Warm plains. Solitary or herd of 6–30. Always neutral, no treasure. Advancement 12–22 HD (Huge). No level adjustment.

lines: Constrict. Melee weapon attack +6 against one creature anywhere in the room. Hit for 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage and grapple the creature, escape DC 16. gm.title: Encounter
lines: The creature on the far side senses arrivals through tremors in the room. Each character makes a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice the water ripple before the tentacle appears. A character who knows the room’s story or detects the local magic gets advantage. Failure leaves the character surprised. On a grapple the tentacle immediately pulls the target into sewage 3 ft. deep. If the grapple persists on the following round, it pulls the target underwater in the 10-ft. section. It then has three-quarters cover, and the target cannot breathe. An unconscious target grappled underwater is pulled through the planar rupture and devoured.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A large tawny animal with the head, chest, and clawed forelegs of a lion and the hindquarters of a horse. The portrait depicts a maned adult.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Descending AC 5. THAC0 15. Three basic attacks per round. Steady morale (11–12). Semi-intelligence (2–4). No magic resistance. Size L, 10 ft. long. No treasure.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: TSR 2524, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix, printed pp. 32–33.

gm.title: Attacks
lines:
Claws and bite. Two front claws for 1d6 each and one bite for 1d10. A bonded mount seldom uses claws while ridden. It fiercely attacks with claw and bite if its rider falls.
Kick. A stationary feliquine can kick for 2d6 with its hind legs. It cannot also use its front claws in that round. Wild ones kick when cornered, while trained mounts can use it in combat.

gm.title: Defenses and Legacy
lines: Add +1 to all surprise rolls. Feliquines sometimes gain a Legacy and need no cinnabryl to avoid Affliction. XP is 420 with a Legacy. The compendium’s general monster Legacy rules allow three uses per day once fully active and immediate use once activated. The initial week permits one use per day. Its powers fade after leaving the Red Curse and Haze. See printed pp. 6–9.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Uncommon temperate-steppe carnivore, active at any time. Pride organization and 3d4 appearing. Females may herd prey toward males, or attack directly. Herd mammals and horses are usual prey. Only rakastas and occasionally elves form rider bonds. A bonded mount may carry a wounded rider to safety, and must periodically be released to hunt and mate to remain manageable.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A 30-foot lizard that resembles a wingless red dragon. It has gray scales, a back mottled with red and brown, and a reddish underside. Hatchlings are light gray and darken with age.

gm.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Claws and bite · Its regular attacks are two raking claws and a bite.

Fiery cone · It can breathe fire simultaneously with its claws and bite. The cone is 15 feet long, 5 feet wide at the mouth, and 10 feet wide at the end. It deals 2–12 fire damage, halved by a successful save vs. breath weapon.
Fire immunity · It is immune to fire-based attacks.

gm.title: Lair mechanics
lines: Hunting cycle · It sleeps about half the time and leaves its lair every fortnight to hunt. It carries prey back and collects shiny objects.
Eggs · A lair has a 10% chance to contain 1–4 eggs. Young lizards leave to hunt after hatching.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: 1–4 appearing. Very rare. Solitary organization. Day activity. Carnivorous and neutral.
Animal intelligence (1). Treasure B, Q (×10), S, T. Steady (11–12) morale. Magic resistance Nil.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A mottled flying ray that lies buried under forest litter until prey comes close.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any forest. Rare, solitary, active at any time. Carnivore. Intelligence 0. Treasure J–N ×10, Q ×5, X. Neutral. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Wingspan 16–20 feet. Elite morale 13–14.

gm.title: Hit dice, THAC0 and XP
lines: 8 HD has THAC0 13 and 3,000 XP. 9 HD has THAC0 11 and 4,000 XP. 10 HD has THAC0 11 and 5,000 XP. 11 HD has THAC0 9 and 6,000 XP. Add 1,000 XP if it has a Legacy.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. One attack for 3d4 damage. Against a human-sized or smaller target, a hit that beats the required attack roll by more than 2 swallows the target. The swallowed target dies at the end of six rounds. It can attack the ray from inside using a dagger or short sword at −4 to hit against the ray’s normal AC.
Sting. Instead of biting, make one sting attack for 2d10 damage. The target must save vs. paralyzation or be stunned for 2d4 rounds.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Buried ambush grants +2 to surprise opponents. Flies no higher than the treetops and can turn sideways to pass between trees. Changing its coloration takes several days.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: A Legacy occurs 25% of the time, usually from Region 4, such as Duplicate or Regenerate. The text also gives a 10% chance of a Region 3 Legacy. Forest rays need no cinnabryl.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The swallow rule says the roll must exceed the required number by more than 2, but the example lets a 16 swallow when the target number is 14. This block uses the written threshold.

gm.title: Attack
lines: Bite +11 melee for 2d8 + 12 damage, or Tail Slap +11 melee for 1d12 + 12 damage.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: One Bite +11 melee for 2d8 + 12 damage, or one Tail Slap +11 melee for 1d12 + 12 damage.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Hold Breath (Ex). It can hold its breath for four times its Constitution score, or 76 rounds, before it risks drowning.
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Skills. Hide +1, Listen +5, Spot +5, Swim +16. In water, add a +4 racial bonus to Hide. At the surface with only eyes and nostrils exposed, it also gets +10 cover to Hide. The +8 racial Swim bonus applies to special actions and hazards. It can take 10 on Swim while distracted or endangered, and can run when swimming in a straight line.
Feats. Alertness, Endurance, Skill Focus (Hide). Endurance adds +4 to Constitution checks to hold breath after the listed interval.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Environment. Warm marshes, Salt water. Organization. Solitary or colony (6–11). Giant crocodiles use the smaller crocodile’s ambush behavior, waiting low in the water and trying to drag a grabbed victim deeper. Treasure none. Advancement. 8–14 HD (Huge). Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Improved Grab (Ex). After it hits a Large or smaller foe with Bite, the crocodile can immediately attempt a grapple as a free action without a touch attack or an attack of opportunity. On a win, it draws the target into its space and may drag it if the victim is within its drag limit. It can grapple normally or hold with its jaws at −20 on grapple checks to avoid becoming grappled itself. Winning the initial grab adds no damage. Later successful grapple checks with the hold deal Bite damage. The crocodile uses opposed grapple checks to pin or move a struggling target.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A target escapes with an opposed grapple check in place of an attack or a standard-action Escape Artist check against the crocodile’s grapple check. Escaping a pin leaves the target in the grapple. After the crocodile’s breath-holding interval, use escalating Constitution checks beginning at DC 10. Failure starts drowning, with 0 HP and unconsciousness on the first round, −1 HP on the next, and death on the third.

gm.title: Figurine mechanics
lines: Activation · Use an action to speak the command word and throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 ft. The fly appears if the space is free and large enough.

gm.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Tongue · Its sticky tongue reaches three times its body length and gains a +4 bonus to the attack roll. A hit causes no direct damage. The target gets one chance to strike the tongue before being reeled in. A hit frees the target, and the frog leaves that target alone.

Reeling in prey · A lighter victim is drawn in during the round they miss the tongue. A heavier victim takes one extra round and gets another chance to hit the tongue. A victim more than twice the frog’s weight cannot be drawn in and is released on the third round after capture. The text leaves equal weight unspecified.
First bite · A successful bite in the first round the victim is in reach deals the maximum damage for the frog’s Hit Dice.

Swallow whole · An attack roll of 20 can swallow a victim shorter than 3 feet. A victim has three rounds to escape before asphyxiating. An attack roll of 18 or higher with an edged weapon lets the victim cut their way out. A successful escape kills the frog. Damage dealt to the frog has a 33% chance to also affect the swallowed victim.

gm.title: Summoning
lines: Giant Insect is a level 4 Druid conjuration. It takes an action to cast, requires verbal and somatic components, and lasts up to 10 minutes with concentration. Choose a giant centipede, spider, or wasp at casting. It appears in an unoccupied space the caster can see within 60 ft. and vanishes at 0 HP or when the spell ends.

gm.title: Initiative and commands
lines: The summoned creature is allied with the caster and the caster’s allies. It acts on the caster’s initiative count, immediately after the caster. Verbal commands cost the caster no action. Without orders, the insect takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

gm.title: Scaling
lines: Use the slot level for the spell level in these formulas. AC equals 11 + spell level. HP equals 30 + 10 per spell level above 4. Its Proficiency Bonus equals the caster’s. The block gives no CR and 0 XP.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Large Beast, Unaligned. STR 17 (+3), DEX 13 (+1), CON 15 (+2), INT 4 (−3), WIS 14 (+2), CHA 3 (−4). The saving throw modifiers match these six modifiers. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12. The insect understands its caster’s languages.

gm.title: Movement
lines: Walk 40 ft. and climb 40 ft. The wasp form also flies 40 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Spider Climb. The insect climbs difficult surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make half the spell level in attacks, rounded down.
Poison Jab. Melee attack roll using the caster’s spell attack modifier, with 10-ft. reach. A hit deals 1d6 + 3 + spell level piercing damage and 1d4 poison damage.
Web Bolt (Spider only). Ranged attack roll using the caster’s spell attack modifier, with 60-ft. range. A hit deals 1d10 + 3 + spell level bludgeoning damage and reduces the target’s Speed to 0 until the start of the insect’s next turn.

lines: Venomous Spew (Centipede only). One creature the centipede can see within 10 ft. makes a Constitution saving throw against the caster’s spell save DC. On a failure it is Poisoned until the start of the insect’s next turn.

lines: The first printing applied the extra 10 HP per spell level. The official correction applies the increase only for levels above 4. This summary uses the corrected formula.

lines:
DC 12 Perception notices the rats chattering and moving among the shadows. Thirteen rats begin above the party and move in groups of three or four. They target isolated PCs, such as someone more than 4 squares from allies or out of their line of sight.
A rat starting on the ground spends a move action to reach the stalactite ceiling. On the ceiling it uses climb speed and gains superior cover against nonadjacent opponents. The cavern’s dense rocks give rats cover against adjacent foes and can block a PC’s line of sight to a rat while the rat sees the PC. Rats can roll Stealth when they have cover and cross the encounter’s difficult terrain at normal speed.
The adventure offers an optional ceiling rule. A rat can share a square with a character while above them, then attack while dropping to an adjacent square. It must leave the ceiling to attack this way. A DC 20 Perception check detects the false wall of the secret chamber.
