gm.title: Appearance
lines: An immense rust-brown squid with a long pointed mantle, paired fins, eight short arms, and two longer club-tipped feeding tentacles.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC 17 (−2 size, +3 Dex, +6 natural). Touch AC 11. Flat-footed AC 14. Base attack +9. Grapple +29. Space 15 ft. Reach 15 ft., or 30 ft. with a tentacle. Fort +9, Ref +11, Will +5. Low-light vision.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD. MonstersAnimals.rtf, SQUID, GIANT. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/squidGiant.htm

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Ten tentacles +15 melee, each for 1d6 + 8, and bite +10 melee for 2d8 + 4.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Improved Grab (Ex). A tentacle hit against an opponent of any size can start a grapple as a free action and without provoking an attack of opportunity. A successful grapple check establishes a hold and allows constriction. The squid’s +4 racial grapple bonus is accounted for in the printed +29.
Constrict (Ex). Deal 1d6 + 8 damage on a successful grapple check.
Sundering tentacles. A foe can sunder a tentacle as though it were a weapon. Each tentacle has 10 HP. If that limb holds a target, the squid usually makes its attack of opportunity with a different limb. Severing a tentacle deals 5 damage to the squid. It typically retreats after losing five tentacles. A severed limb regrows in 1d10 + 10 days.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. Aquatic subtype. Breathes water and has no amphibious quality. Normal swimming needs no Swim check.
Ink Cloud (Ex). Once per minute as a free action, release a 20-ft. cube of ink. The cloud blocks all vision within it and gives total concealment.
Jet (Ex). Once per round, use a full-round action to jet backward 320 ft. in a straight line without provoking attacks of opportunity.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Listen +10, Spot +11, Swim +16. Gain a +8 racial bonus on Swim checks for special actions or hazards. You may take 10 while distracted or endangered and run while swimming in a straight line.
Feats: Alertness, Diehard, Endurance, Toughness twice.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Temperate aquatic. Solitary. Advancement is 13–18 HD (Huge) or 19–36 HD (Gargantuan). Level adjustment and treasure are absent. The source describes a predator whose body can exceed 20 ft. in length.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack. The lizard can replace either one with Swallow.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage and grapples the target (escape DC 15). The target remains restrained and the lizard cannot bite a different target until that grapple ends.

Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target the lizard is not grappling. A hit deals 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.

Swallow. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature the lizard is grappling. On a hit the target takes 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage, is swallowed, and is released from the grapple. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the lizard, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each lizard turn. The lizard can hold one swallowed target at a time. If the lizard dies, the swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.

lines:

Combat behavior. Its first target is usually the largest opponent. It turns on an opponent who deals repeated heavy damage or deals more than 15 HP of damage in a round. The voat continues fighting until its opponents are dead.

gm.title: Red Curse and Legacies
lines:
It gains multiple Region 1 Legacies and does not require cinnabryl. The appendix names Amber Paralysis, War Cry, and Weapon Hand as common, with no fixed selection or number. The general appendix rule allows Legacies three times per day for established powers, with immediate use when activated.
Amber Paralysis. Choose a target within 10 yards. On a failed save vs. paralyzation, it is immobilized for 2 rounds per level. The save is penalized by 1 per 3 caster HD, per the appendix.
War Cry. Instantaneous, 10 yards per caster HD, maximum 150 yards. A failed save vs. paralyzation prevents attacking for 1d4 rounds. Fear immunity offers no protection. This Legacy is separate from the native 30-yard screech.
Weapon Hand. One hand becomes a melee weapon that deals 1d8 damage, for 1 round per level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A small scent hound trained to track and flush quarry.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Bite · melee · +4 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 1d8 + 2 piercing

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Diligent Tracker · The hound has advantage on WIS (Survival) checks to track creatures.
Heightened Hearing and Smell · Use Perception 18 when relying on hearing or smell.

gm.title: Action mechanics
lines: Bite · A hit grapples a Medium or smaller target (escape DC 12). While holding it, the hound cannot bite another target.

gm.title: Bonus action mechanics
lines: Flushing Bark · In a 15-ft. cone, creatures that are hiding or behind cover make a DC 12 WIS save. Those that fail immediately stop hiding or move up to 10 ft. out of cover. This forced movement avoids opportunity attacks and damaging terrain.
Swift Hunter · The hound moves up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.

gm.title: Companion use mechanics
lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 50 gp. It can carry 210 lb.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 12. Ability modifiers are STR +1, DEX +2, CON +1, INT −4, WIS +1 and CHA −2. No languages or special senses.
The book prints CR 1/4. The publisher’s index rounds it to 0.3.
The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–144.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: 5–30 appearing. Common. No intelligence (0). Unsteady (5–7) morale. Active at any time, carnivorous, and neutral. No special defenses or magic resistance.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Trip (Ex). After a bite hits, the hyena can use a free action to make a trip attempt at +2. Skip the melee touch attack, and the attempt provokes no attack of opportunity. Success leaves the opponent prone. Standing takes a move action. Oppose the listed modifier with the defender’s better Strength or Dexterity check, applying the normal size and stability modifiers. Normal Trip allows a target up to one size category larger. A failed attempt here gives the defender no counter-trip.

lines: Low-light vision retains color and detail at twice normal human range in dim light. Scent detects creatures within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. lines: Warm deserts. Solitary, pair or pack of 7–16. The source describes a striped hyena about 3 ft. long and 120 lb. Hunters often split into a frontal group and a second group that circles to flank or attack from behind. Always neutral. No treasure.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A white-furred giant ice spider with small red eyes. The queen and ice spider share the species portrait.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Blindsight 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. Languages none. AC 14 from natural armor. Damage resistance cold.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Storm King's Thunder p. 128, Chapter 4, Eye of the All-Father, area 9B Nest. Base rules from the 2014 Monster Manual, Giant Spider, p. 328.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Spider Climb. The spider can climb difficult surfaces and move upside down across ceilings without an ability check.
Web Sense. When touching a web, it knows the location of other creatures in contact with that web.
Web Walker. Webbing does not restrict its movement.
Cold Aura. A creature starting its turn within 5 ft. of the queen takes 5 (2d4) cold damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit for 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The creature must make a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If that poison damage reduces it to 0 HP, it becomes stable and remains poisoned for 1 hour even if it regains HP. It is paralyzed while poisoned by this effect.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. On a hit the web restrains the target. While restrained by it, the target takes 2 (1d4) cold damage at the start of each of its turns. The restrained creature can use its action to burst the web with a DC 12 Strength check. The web has AC 10 and 5 HP, is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to poison and psychic damage. Bludgeoning damage works normally against it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: If the queen dies in the nest, her 32 eggs hatch immediately and form a Swarm of Insects (Spiders) with cold resistance. The swarm acts on the queen’s initiative. If there is no foe to attack, it begins to eat the queen’s remains. After Web is used, roll a d6 at the start of each of the spider’s turns. A 5 or 6 restores the use, as does a short or long rest.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Three attacks per round at THAC0 15: two claw attacks for 1d8 each and a bite for 2d6.

gm.title: Special rules
lines:
Rush. When prey is visible and less than 10 yards away, the juhrion drops stealth and charges. Movement rises from 12 to 18 for short fighting bursts.
Maul. If both claws hit the same creature in a single round, the juhrion pins it under its weight and keeps clawing and biting. The victim loses any Dexterity bonus to AC, can use no weapon larger than a dagger against the juhrion, and has its casting fouled. Legacies still function if they need no movement. A successful Bend Bars roll frees the victim.
Vermilia. A claw attack carries the printed 50% chance of infection. The referenced Parasite entry allows living creatures a save vs. poison to avoid infection. Undead are infected automatically on exposure and can save vs. death magic each day, with a penalty equal to that day’s vermilia damage, to avoid the damage for that day. Apply −1 per Legacy on saves associated with infection. The infection deals 1 HP on day one, then 2, 4, 8 and so on, doubling each day until cured. Cure disease or heal is printed as treatment. It counts as a +2 magical weapon when damaging undead or magical creatures. The juhrion itself is immune.

gm.title: Red Curse and Legacies

gm.title: Fishing in Icewind Dale
lines: Under the lake procedure on p. 11, use fishing tackle from a rowboat or fish through a hole cut in the ice with a saw or similar tool. After each hour, a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check hooks a trout. Then contest the angler’s Strength (Athletics) against the trout’s Strength check, which the trout makes with advantage. lines:

Toxic Spikes. Ranged, standard, Poison, recharge 5–6. Make two ranged 5 attacks against two different targets, each at +7 vs. AC. A hit deals 1d8 + 4 damage, inflicts ongoing 5 poison damage and slows the target. One save ends both effects on that target.

gm.title: Encounter checks
lines:
DC 15 Nature identifies a kruthik in the open pit. DC 12 Perception catches its musk. DC 17 Perception notices raised floor sections. A PC actively searching can locate a hidden pit with DC 20 Perception. The kruthiks avoid those trap squares. A triggered trap drops a PC for 1d10 damage and works once. Climbing out takes DC 15 Athletics. Jumping over takes DC 20 Athletics from standing or DC 10 with a running start.
The adult opens with Toxic Spikes when the party comes into range and then closes for Claw. Prefer the power’s two different targets as printed. In the 2-ft.-wide lair tunnels Small kruthiks move at full speed and the Medium adult at half speed. Medium or larger PCs cannot fit. A Small PC can squeeze at half speed, grants combat advantage and takes a −5 penalty on attacks until back in open space. Squeezing provokes opportunity attacks from adjacent foes.

gm.title: Printing notes
lines: The stat block prints Wisdom 12 (+4). The usual half-level calculation would give +3. Keep the printed +4. Perception is also printed as +4. The summary on p. 46 broadly says kruthiks move at full speed in their tunnels. The specific tunnel feature on p. 47 distinguishes Small kruthiks at full speed and the Medium adult at half speed.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Warm forests. Solitary or paired. No treasure. Advances to 4–5 HD (Medium). No level adjustment. Usually hunts at night. The source also uses this block for comparably sized cats such as jaguars, panthers and mountain lions.

gm.title: Special attacks and combat
lines:
Improved Grab (Ex). On a bite hit, attempt a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity or making a fresh touch attack. The generic rule limits this to a target at least one size smaller. A win pulls it into the leopard’s space and establishes a hold that allows rake attacks. A hold alone adds no damage. Each successful grapple check in subsequent rounds deals the bite damage. The leopard can hold using only its bite at −20 to its grapple checks, leaving itself free of the grapple while it holds the foe.
Pounce (Ex). Charge and make a full attack that includes two rake attacks.
Rake (Ex). +6 melee, 1d3+1. The general rake rule normally requires beginning the turn already grappling and removes the usual −4 penalty to natural attacks in a grapple. Pounce explicitly includes two rakes on its charge.

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Scent (Ex) · Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.
Carrying capacity · Light up to 150 lb., medium 151–300 lb., heavy 301–450 lb. Can drag 2,250 lb.

Mounted combat · The horse cannot fight while carrying a rider. It rarely attacks with its hooves. The listed secondary hoof attack adds half its Strength modifier to damage. A rider controlling it in battle makes a DC 20 Ride check as a move action.
Run · Run at five times speed with up to medium armor and load, or four times with heavy armor or load. Add +4 to Jump with a running start. Keep the Dexterity bonus to AC.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Domesticated or herd (6–30).

Endurance grants +4 on endurance and exposure checks and saves, including Swim to resist nonlethal damage and Constitution checks for continuing to run, forced marches, holding breath, and avoiding starvation or thirst.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: A Dazed creature can do one of the following on its turn: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. If it becomes Dazed during its turn, the turn ends. Extra actions granted by effects such as Haste or Action Surge remain available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration remove the condition. The GM can allow other remedies.

Running Leap. After a 10-ft. running start, the lion can long jump up to 25 ft.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A tawny lion with a heavy dark mane, broad paws, and a long tufted tail.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, LION. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/lion.htm

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC 15 (−1 size, +3 Dexterity, +3 natural armor), touch 12, flat-footed 12. Base attack +3, grapple +12. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Two claws at melee +7 each for 1d4 + 5 damage apiece and one bite at melee +2 for 1d8 + 2 damage.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Pounce (Ex). A charge can end in a full attack plus two rake attacks.
Improved Grab (Ex). After a bite hit against a smaller foe, attempt to grapple as a free action without a touch attack or opportunity attack. A success pulls the target into the lion’s space and establishes a hold. The lion may grapple normally or hold with only its bite at −20 on grapple checks while remaining free to threaten and use its other attacks. In later rounds, a successful grapple check deals bite damage. The lion’s entry also permits raking after a hold.
Rake (Ex). Each rake is melee +7 for 1d4 + 2 damage. The general Rake rule grants the two additional attacks against a grappled foe and says the lion must start its turn grappling. Rake bypasses the usual −4 natural-weapon penalty in a grapple. Pounce expressly includes its two rakes.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light.
Scent (Ex). Detect normal odors within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. Finding the direction takes a move action. Within 5 ft., pinpoint the source.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Balance +7, Hide +3, Listen +5, Move Silently +11, Spot +5. Racial bonuses of +4 to Balance, Hide, and Move Silently are included. In tall grass or heavy undergrowth, the Hide racial bonus becomes +12.
Feats: Alertness, Run.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Warm plains. Solitary, pair, or pride of 6–10. Advancement 6–8 HD (Large). Level adjustment —. Male African lions are 5–8 ft. long and 330–550 lb. Females are somewhat smaller and use the same statistics.

gm.title: Timing note
lines: The Lion entry permits a rake after winning its Improved Grab check but gives no timing. The general Rake rule requires starting the turn grappling. The charge from Pounce specifically includes the two rake attacks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A bear that picks up scents through snow, water, or soil and knocks foes down with a heavy swat.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception +3, Survival +3. Passive Perception 13. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exceptional Smell. Add +10 to Wisdom (Perception) checks that use smell. Soil, snow, and water do not block the bear's sense of smell.
Natural Camouflage. The beast has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in its native terrain.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. Use the maximum damage against a Plant instead of rolling.
Swat. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing or bludgeoning damage, chosen by the bear. The target falls Prone if it fails a DC 13 Strength save.

gm.title: Optional Bear Features
lines:
Adept Climber (black or spectacled bear). Gain a climb speed of 25 ft.
Arctic Traveler (polar bear). Gain advantage on saves against Exhaustion, tolerate temperatures as low as −50°F, and ignore difficult terrain from ice or snow.
Fearsome Growl (any bear, bonus action, 1/day). Each creature within 15 ft. that hears the bear makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is Frightened of the bear until the end of the bear's next turn. On a success, it is immune to all bears' Fearsome Growl for 24 hours.
Clever Claws (sloth bear). Use claws in place of thieves' tools to open locks and add +3 to the Dexterity check.
Powerful Jaws (giant panda or sun bear). Bite deals an extra 4 (1d8) damage. Use maximum damage against Plants. This option prevents the bear from using Multiattack.
Sprint (black, brown, polar, spectacled, or sun bear, recharges after a short or long rest). When the bear moves on its turn in combat, it can triple its speed until the turn ends.

gm.title: Description
lines: A small feline ambusher that can drop from a tree without injury and pounce from cover.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Acrobatics +4, Perception +6, Stealth +6. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 16. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Agile Landing. The cat takes no damage from falling 40 ft. or less unless it is Incapacitated.
Hunter's Pounce. A hit with advantage grapples a Small or smaller target (escape DC 12). The cat cannot attack another creature while holding the target this way.
Natural Camouflage. The beast has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in its native terrain.
Sprint (recharges after a short or long rest). When the cat moves on its turn in combat, it can triple its speed until the turn ends.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) piercing damage against a Grappled or Restrained target.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) slashing damage if the attack had advantage.

gm.title: Optional Wildcat Features
lines:
Adept Climber (clouded leopard, jaguar, leopard, lynx, or snow leopard). Gain a climb speed of 25 ft.
Agile Landing (any Medium wildcat). Ignore falls of 40 ft. or less unless Incapacitated.
Deadly Bite (lion, tiger, or jaguar). A Bite hit against a Prone target is a critical hit.
Desert Dweller (sand cat). Ignore difficult terrain from dirt or sand and tolerate temperatures up to 120°F. Fresh food meets the cat's need for water.
Mountain Dweller (lynx or snow leopard). Ignore difficult terrain from snow, ice, or steep slopes.
Superior Sprint (cheetah or sand cat, 2 uses per short or long rest). When the cat moves on its turn in combat, it can quadruple its speed until the turn ends. Replaces Sprint.
Pack Tactics (lion). The cat has advantage on attacks against a target within 5 ft. of at least one ally of the cat, as long as the ally is not Incapacitated.
Powerful Leap (caracal, cougar, lion, margay, serval, or snow leopard). Double all jump distances, with or without a running start. Use either Strength or Dexterity to determine the distance.
Swimmer (tiger, leopard, ocelot, or jaguar). Gain a swim speed of 30 ft.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.

lines: A powerful gray winged wolf with a bushy tail, pale underside, and broad furred wings.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Descending AC. Low intelligence (5–7). Elite morale 13–14. Treasures, special defenses, and magic resistance nil.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: TSR, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix (1996), Lupasus, printed pp. 68–69.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One attack at THAC0 15 for 2d6 damage.

gm.title: Special rules
lines: Flight. It can carry up to 200 lb. in flight. Unencumbered, save vs. paralyzation after each hour of flight. A failed save forces half an hour of rest per two previous hours of flight. A rider lowers maneuverability from C to D and calls for a save every half hour. After losing 50% or more of its HP, it cannot fly. It can glide until it has lost 75% or more. Wings are covered with fine fur and have the same vulnerability to fire as the rest of the body. Under the appendix’s maneuverability rules, C and D must maintain at least half their speed to stay aloft. C can turn up to 90 degrees per round and attack once every two rounds. A creature that touches the web is caught as in a net and cannot move away from the doorway. A weapon that touches it sticks and needs a DC 16 Strength check to free.

Ceiling ambush · The spider attacks, with surprise if possible, when someone is caught in or attacks the doorway web. It always attacks the nearest target. It throws a web only when no character is currently entangled in a web.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Blood Frenzy. The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Water Breathing. The shark breathes only underwater.
Silver Spear. While the spear is lodged in its side, the shark sheds bright silver light within 10 ft. and dim light for another 10 ft. A character within 5 ft. can use an action to dislodge the spear with a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check.

lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.

lines: Spear-assisted swim. While the spear is embedded, if the shark uses its action to Bite and misses, it can spend a bonus action to swim up to 25 ft. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

lines: The rope holding the amulet has AC 17 and 5 HP, and characters can attack it to cut the amulet free. If the shark is dead or incapacitated, a character can remove the rope as an action.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: The Moonshark prowls the final chamber of Jigow’s Emerald Grotto. It attacks creatures entering its chamber.

gm.title: Encounter application
lines: If the party crossed the grotto in 10 rounds or fewer, the rivals arrive after the shark encounter. At 11 to 15 rounds, the rivals enter and roll initiative in round 3. Unless hostile to the characters, they help fight the shark. Hostile rivals pursue the amulet or interfere with the characters without intentionally killing them. At 16 rounds or more, the rivals arrive first and reduce the shark to 75 HP before the characters roll initiative. At 0 HP the shark knocks over the southern pillar, breaking open the passage to E11.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The adventure inherits the Giant Shark block and gives effects tied to a removable spear. The Huge Beast classification comes from the 2014 parent block.

lines: Spitting · An ill-tempered camel has a 50% chance to spit at someone who tries to ride it or use it as a pack animal. The victim then has a 25% chance of being blinded for 1–3 rounds.

Herd stampede · A frightened herd has a 25% chance of stampeding. Roll 2d4 camels for each creature in its path that fails to take cover. Each camel deals 1–4 damage to that creature. Trampled creatures stay down until the herd passes.

gm.title: Physical attacks mechanics
lines: Bite and wing claws · Bite for 1d4, and rake once with each wing claw for 1d2 per rake.
Tail slash or stab · Choose a slash for 1d6 or a stab for 3d4.

lines: Ambush · It flies low and uses terrain as cover. Its loud calls when excited make surprise uncommon.
Lair counts · The table gives 1–12 appearing and 1–30 in a lair. The prose says lairs usually hold over 30.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Also called dragazhar. Uncommon pack hunter. Nocturnal above ground and active at any time underground. Carnivore. Average to high intelligence (8–14). Neutral evil. Steady (11) morale. Treasure M, O, Z in lair. The table lists no special attacks, special defenses, or magic resistance.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A low, long, turtlelike animal with olive leathery skin, flush bony plates beneath the back, brown and yellow spots, broad feet and large black eyes. Adults reach 10 to 12 ft. long.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC 5, or 6 against attacks near the legs. Morale average (8–10). Animal intelligence (1). No treasure or magic resistance. The entry gives no special saving throw.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix, pp. 78–79.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One bite per round, 3d4 damage. On an unmodified roll of 20, the bite severs a hand or foot from an attacking human-sized or smaller creature. The entry gives no separate save against severing. It rarely bites without severe provocation unless trained to attack on command.

gm.title: Armor and movement
lines: Head and back are AC 5. Opponents near the extremities are treated as targeting the legs at AC 6. It has no shell to retract into. A male out of water takes a −2 penalty on attack rolls and 2 damage per round from dryness. They can run for days without rest and keep swimming indefinitely at half movement. Maximum load is 600 lb. at full speed, 900 lb. at half speed or 1,200 lb. at one-third speed.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Nikt’oos gain Legacies and need cinnabryl to avert Affliction. Most have little access to it, so Affliction is common. The entry gives no fixed Legacy.

gm.title: Encounters and ecology
lines: Uncommon, solitary, one appearing. Active by day. Tortles and snappers often domesticate them as amphibious mounts or beasts of burden. Wild ones usually flee humanoids but become aggressive in mating season. A female buries 5d6 eggs yearly above the high tide line on a warm beach. Males normally stay in water and may come ashore to defend an egg-laying female. They eat jellyfish, mollusks and seaweed. Adults live about 90 years in the wild or up to 150 in captivity. Fewer than 5% of wild offspring reach adulthood.

lines: A large toad with a broad mouth, warty back, and heavy hind legs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Immune to cold damage. Darkvision 30 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Explorer's Guide to Wildemount, March 2020 first printing, Frozen Sick, C5 Old Croaker's Pool, p. 240. https://fliphtml5.com/DnD5E/Explorers-Guide-To-Wildemount/Explorers_Guide_To_Wildemount/241/

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Old Croaker breathes air and water.
Standing Leap. With or without a run, it can long jump 20 ft. or high jump 10 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 5 (1d10) poison damage and grapples the target, escape DC 13. Until the grapple ends, that target is restrained and Old Croaker can bite only that target.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack on a grappled target of Medium size or smaller. A hit ends the grapple and swallows the target. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside attacks and effects, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of Old Croaker’s turns. Old Croaker holds one swallowed target at once. When Old Croaker dies, the creature is no longer restrained and can move 5 ft. to emerge prone.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Old Croaker lurks under the freezing pool in Croaker Cave. Hulil trained it to ferry visitors across the pool one at a time.

gm.title: Encounter application
lines: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check can persuade Old Croaker to leave the party alone and carry the characters across individually.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The encounter changes the Giant Toad on Monster Manual p. 329 by granting cold damage immunity. D&D Beyond publishes this encounter variant as its own sheet.

gm.title: Traits mechanics
lines: Heightened Hearing and Smell · Perception is 16 for hearing or smell.

gm.title: Actions mechanics
lines: Multiattack · 2 attacks · The olhund makes one Smashing Paw attack and one Bite attack.
Bite · +5 to hit · reach 5 ft. · One target takes 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage on a hit. · 1d8 + 3 piercing

Smashing Paw · +5 to hit · reach 5 ft. · One target takes 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature no more than one size larger falls prone on a failed save. The olhund can choose to knock a creature unconscious instead of killing it. · DC 14 Strength · 1d4 + 3 bludgeoning

gm.title: Bonus Actions mechanics
lines: Intimidating Rumble · range 30 ft. · Recharge 6 · One creature the olhund can see within 30 ft. is frightened of it for 1 minute on a failed save. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. · DC 13 Charisma

gm.title: Variant options mechanics
lines: Variant selection · Choose at most one option. The GM removes either Smashing Paw or Intimidating Rumble.

Den Tactics (trait) · The olhund has advantage on attacks and ability checks in its den. It can choose or be trained to accept a new den with the Creature Training downtime activity from Player’s Guide 2.

Grappling Charge (trait) · If the olhund moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and then hits with Bite or Smashing Paw on the same turn, the target falls prone and is grappled on a failed save (escape DC 14). It can grapple one target at a time. · DC 14 Strength
Protective Strike (reaction) · When a target the olhund can see is hit by an attack from a creature within 5 ft. of it, the olhund can make one Bite attack against the attacker.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Printed Perception 11, Stealth 16. Ability modifiers are Str +4, Dex +2, Con +4, Int −3, Wis +1, Cha −2.
The article describes the hounds as moving slowly in everyday life. The printed combat speed is 60 ft.
The source gives no replacement Multiattack when the GM removes Smashing Paw.
Protective Strike leaves the reference point for its 5-ft. distance implicit.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: Shaggy mastodon-like beast with heavy forelegs, downward-curving tusks and a trunk too short to fight with. The reused portrait is an unarmored specimen.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Descending armor class. Use the AD&D 1e monster attack matrix for the applicable Hit Dice. Rare. 1–8 appearing, no lair or treasure. Standard magic resistance and no special defenses in the generic block. No psionics. The Appendix leaves Level/XP blank.

gm.title: Tusks and forelegs
lines: Four attacks, each for 3–12 damage, using tusks and forelegs. The trunk cannot be used to fight. The oliphant can engage up to four man-sized foes, two ogre-sized foes, or one giant-sized foe simultaneously.

gm.title: Chessboard Rook
lines: Use the p. 11 preset for the Rook. Leather armor gives AC 2. Speed 15″, 10+5 HD, 65 HP and four attacks of 3–12 each. The Rook also has 25% magic resistance.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Avoids inhabited areas when solitary. A young specimen can be captured and trained, with mature trained males especially effective. War animals can wear reinforced armor and spikes and carry archers or pikemen in howdahs. Regular fire does not scare the animal unless the fire directly threatens it. When threatened an oliphant generally fights instead of fleeing.

gm.title: Groups and value
lines: When three or more appear, check each animal beyond the first two. The module gives a 25% chance of a calf and 75% for a half-grown animal. Young are split evenly between the sexes. A solitary animal is male, and any group has at most one mature male. Tusks are worth 100–400 gp each. Ivory is worth about 4 gp per pound.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The generic oliphant and Chessboard Rook share the profile. The armor, fixed HP and 25% magic resistance are encounter-specific.
Generic oliphant level and XP are blank on p. 30. No numeric morale is printed.

lines: A gray-brown pachyderm with four curved tusks, a short trunk and broad round ears.

gm.title: Attacks

Stomp · melee · +9 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 3d10 + 6 bludgeoning

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Siege Monster · It deals double damage to objects and structures.
Terrifying Siege · Destroying a Small or larger object forces every hostile creature within 10 ft. to make a DC 16 CHA save. A failed save frightens the creature until the end of its next turn.

Trampling Charge · After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hitting it with Gore that turn, the target must pass a DC 16 STR save or fall prone. The warbeast can Stomp the target once as a bonus action if it is prone.
Condition resistance · The block lists resistance to frightened, prone.

gm.title: Action mechanics
lines: Multiattack · Make one Gore and one Stomp attack or make two Gore attacks.
Stomp · It can target only a prone creature.

gm.title: Bonus action mechanics
lines: Trunk Sweep · Creatures in a 15-ft. cone make a DC 16 STR save or fall prone.

gm.title: Companion use mechanics
lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 2,400 gp. It can carry 1,560 lb.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 9. Ability modifiers are STR +9, DEX −1, CON +5, INT −4, WIS +0 and CHA −2. No languages or special senses.
The book spells it Oliphaunt Warbeast. The profile uses the existing catalog name and keeps the printed attack bonuses and damage.
The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.

gm.title: Hit point rule

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A large gray or black manatee relative with a flattened horizontal tail, short foreflippers ending in small webbed hands, and no external hind legs. Its small head has a straight snout and a bristly split upper lip. Males have two small tusklike incisors. Adults reach 9 to 11 ft. and up to 1,300 lb.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC 6 (10 unarmored). Morale steady (11–12). Low to very intelligent (5–12). Treasure K (F). No special defenses or magic resistance. The entry gives no individual saving throw values.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix, pp. 81–82.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One weapon attack per round for 1d8 damage. Omm-was favor nets underwater and use spears and tridents for defense. Some traded with Herathians for underwater crossbows.

gm.title: Burn Legacy
lines: Most omm-was have Burn. It activates as an instantaneous Legacy up to three times per day. A successful attack roll deals 1d4 plus 1 per level or HD. At the typical 3 HD that is 1d4 + 3 with a 2-ft. range. The range starts at touch and increases 1 ft. per level beyond first to 10 ft. maximum. The flame comes from a fixed hand or mouth and may ignite a flammable object even when the attack misses the target. Omm-was need cinnabryl to ward off Affliction. An omm-wa Afflicted with Burn overheats after a few seconds out of the water.

gm.title: Movement and senses
lines: Air-breathing and at home in salt or fresh water. It can leave the water for at most 30 minutes at a time. It sees more than 300 ft. in clear water and roughly as far as a human in air, though bright light bothers its eyes. It rarely dives below 100 ft.

gm.title: Encounter groups
lines: Rare, any activity cycle. Roll 1d4 + 2 or 1d6 + 14 appearing. A family includes one female shaman of levels 1–3. For every 30 omm-was add a fighter of levels 3–5. For every 60 add a warleader of effective fighter levels 5–8. For every 100 add a wise woman of priest levels 4–6. Shamans normally advance as priests to level 8. About one male in five can gain fighter levels. The rare twin pair is one female shaman, maximum level 8, and one male fighter protector, maximum level 10. Males have a 5% chance of a character kit, typically Defender.

gm.title: Society and ecology
lines: Females hold all authority and inherit their rank through the maternal line. Females reach maturity at 12. The family herbivores tend underwater farms and feed mainly at night. They gather mineral nodules, including a little cinnabryl, and record messages with pebble arrangements or knotted strings and beads.

gm.title: Attack
lines: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. At the end of its movement, deal damage automatically to each creature whose space it shares. There is no attack roll or miss chance for concealment or cover. The attack is nonmagical.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. The automatic Swarm Attack uses the same rules in both entries.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Disease (Ex). Filth fever is delivered by the swarm attack. Make an immediate DC 12 Fortitude save to prevent infection. On a failure, after 1d3 days take 1d3 Dex and 1d3 Con damage. Save at DC 12 daily afterward or repeat the ability damage. Two successes in a row clear the disease.
Distraction (Ex). A living creature that begins its turn in the swarm’s square makes a DC 12 Fortitude save or is nauseated for 1 round. A nauseated creature can take only one move action per turn and cannot attack, cast spells or concentrate. The shared subtype wording specifies living creatures vulnerable to the swarm’s damage. Both printed triggers are recorded here.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light, with color and detail.
Scent. Detect by smell out to 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind or 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action gives the direction. Pinpoint the source within 5 ft.
Tiny swarm. Halve damage from slashing and piercing weapons. It cannot be critically hit or flanked. The swarm cannot grapple or be grappled, tripped, or bull rushed. It breaks up at 0 HP or below and does not become staggered or dying from damage. Losing HP above 0 does not reduce its attack or defenses.

gm.title: Swarm movement
lines: One nonflying Tiny swarm represents about 300 rats and uses one set of stats and saves. It can cover any four contiguous squares and fit through gaps a constituent rat can use. It shares spaces with creatures of any size and can pass through them. Moving into or through an opponent’s space can provoke an attack of opportunity. The swarm does not threaten creatures or make attacks of opportunity.

gm.title: Swarm spell and effect rules
lines: Immune to effects that target a fixed number of creatures. The shared mind-affecting exception requires intelligence and a hive mind, and this block lists no hive mind. Area effects deal 50% extra damage. Casting a spell or maintaining concentration in the swarm’s area requires a Concentration check at DC 20 + spell level. Skills requiring patience or focus require a DC 20 Concentration check. An improvised lit torch deals 1d3 fire on a hit, and a broken thrown lit lantern deals 1d4 fire in adjacent squares. A weapon’s added energy damage applies in full. Sufficient damage reduction and incorporeality can prevent the swarm attack’s ordinary damage.

gm.title: Nonlethal dispersal
lines: If nonlethal damage renders the swarm unconscious it disperses until its HP exceed its nonlethal damage.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Balance +10, Climb +10, Hide +14, Listen +6, Spot +7, Swim +10. Racial bonuses are +4 on Hide and Move Silently, +8 on Balance, Climb and Swim. The swarm uses Dex for Climb and Swim. It can take 10 on Climb and Swim even under pressure and can run while swimming straight. Feats are Alertness and Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Any environment. Solitary, pack of 2–4 swarms, or infestation of 7–12 swarms. It surrounds warm-blooded prey. No advancement, level adjustment, or treasure.

gm.title: Printed discrepancies
lines: The RTF gives 13 HP for 4d8, whose usual mean is 18. Use the listed HP 13. The creature and subtype use different phrasing for the Distraction trigger, as shown above.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: War-trained Trip (Ex). A war-trained riding dog can attempt a trip as a free action after a bite hit, without a touch attack or attack of opportunity. Target a Large or smaller foe. Use the dog’s Strength check at +2 against the defender’s better Strength or Dexterity check, with the usual size and stability modifiers. A win makes the target prone. Failure grants the foe no counter-trip. Mounted combat. The dog can attack while carrying a rider. A rider on a war-trained mount can make a DC 10 Ride check as a free action to also attack.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, sees twice as far as a human and keeps color and detail.
Scent. Detect ordinary creatures within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Double those distances for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action identifies the direction, and within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.
Track by scent. Take the Track feat’s usual checks, with DC 10 for a typical fresh trail and +2 DC per hour since it was left. Surface conditions and poor visibility do not affect scent tracking. Odor strength and number of creatures can shift the DC.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Jump +8, Listen +5, Spot +5, Swim +3, Survival +1. Feats. Alertness, Track (bonus feat).
The entry prints a +4 racial Jump bonus and Jump +8 in the table. Survival has a +4 racial bonus when tracking by scent, for +5 total.

Covers breeds such as collies, huskies and St. Bernards. Light load up to 100 lb., medium 101–200 lb., heavy 201–300 lb., and maximum drag 1,500 lb.

lines:
Forest Rot. When the Rotbeast dies, each non-Fungus creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it gains one level of Exhaustion and contracts forest rot.
Forest rot halves the HP a creature recovers by spending Hit Dice or finishing a long rest. It prevents the normal long-rest reduction in Exhaustion. On finishing each long rest, the infected creature makes a DC 13 Constitution save. Failure adds one level of Exhaustion. Success removes one level, and the creature recovers from forest rot if that success leaves its Exhaustion below 1.

lines: An iridescent bird drawn to hosts carrying parasites such as cardinal ticks and Inheritor lice.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare, usually solitary, active by day. Insectivore. Intelligence 1. No treasure or magic resistance. Neutral. Appearing 1, or occasionally a mated pair. Unreliable morale 2–4.

lines:
The bird has no physical attacks and flees danger.

lines: Continual protection from evil in a 10-foot radius. The bird neither gains Legacies nor needs cinnabryl. When it feeds on a host’s parasites, reduce infestation by 1 percentage point per day. It leaves at 5% and will die after a full week without parasites.

gm.title: Encounter rewards
lines: Award 65 XP for a significant encounter, such as hearing its song or hosting the bird. Killing it gives no XP. The text suggests an optional mild curse for killing one, such as −2 to combat rolls and saves or −4 to proficiency checks. A high-level druid may assign penance. Killing one through captivity is rumored to bring an irreversible curse such as permanent Affliction.

lines: The table says 4–5 feet long, while the description calls it hummingbird-sized. Tiny follows the printed size category. The printing gives a three-use limit without saying whether it applies to each spell. This entry uses a shared limit. The belief that its song forbids all violence is a legend.

lines: Scent (Ex) · Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if the creature is upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. A move action reveals the direction. Within 5 ft., the viper can pinpoint the creature.

Swim · The listed Swim modifier includes a +8 racial bonus for hazards and special maneuvers. The viper can take 10 even when distracted or in danger, and can run in a straight line while swimming.

lines: Always neutral. Solitary. The SRD lists no advancement or level adjustment. The viper usually bites defensively and then retreats.

Roll the printed Bite damage. If the result is below 1, the hit deals 1 damage before applying defenses.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One attack per round for 3d4 damage. It charges a bearer of red steel or cinnabryl, often with Spikes active, and ignores the trick of distracting it with a few dropped red steel spikes.

gm.title: Eating metal
lines: Detects cinnabryl, red steel and steel seed by scent from up to 90 ft. Make a successful attack roll to touch an item made of these metals. On contact it immediately crumbles into edible powder. A weapon of one of those metals that hits the succulus makes contact and is subject to the same disintegration procedure. A magical item with a listed weapon or armor bonus has a 10% chance per +1 to resist. Other magical items made from the listed metals count as +2 (20%). Feeding takes one round regardless of the meal size.

gm.title: Dig and Spikes Legacies
lines: Both are always present. Each is usable three times a day. Digging removes a 5-ft. cube of earth, sand or mud within 10 ft. in one round. A creature within 1 ft. of the pit must pass a Dexterity check or fall inside. A pit in loose earth or mud soon collapses. The appendix’s monster Spikes rules last one round per HD (five rounds). A creature touching the caster takes 2d4 damage. Add 1d6 to a natural physical attack other than a bite. A cinnabryl-rich diet usually protects the succulus from Affliction.

gm.title: Encounters and ecology
lines: Rare family group of 1d12, active by day. Most are encountered with wild swine. Each encounter has a 5% chance of one half-strength offspring, with no separate juvenile stat block in the book. Two succuli produce a succulus. Offspring of a succulus and wild swine have a 5% chance to be a succulus. Eats ore but prefers refined metal. The metal-laden flesh is inedible. Cured hide can make armor equivalent to studded leather (AC 7). A trained young succulus can locate cinnabryl deposits.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The creature entry calls the two Legacies Dig and Spikes, and uses singular Spike in the combat prose. Digging is the Campaign Book name. This profile uses the appendix’s monster form of Spikes.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A dark grey dust bunny that blends into ordinary floor dust. Colonies look like several loose clumps of lint.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: 4d6 appearing. Very rare. Colony. Any activity cycle. Animal intelligence (1). Unreliable morale (2–4). No treasure or magic resistance.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: TSR, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix (1996), pp. 112–113.

gm.title: Combat
lines: One attack, 0 direct damage. A trosip attacks only sleepers and stays still whenever someone is awake within the range of its senses. It senses motion and vibration out to 60 ft., including invisible creatures. It moves silently 95% of the time.

gm.title: Suffocation
lines: At least four trosips are needed to attack one man-sized sleeper effectively. The victim saves vs. paralyzation using only magical protection bonuses. A failed save means death from suffocation in 1d4 + 1 rounds. A success wakes the victim in time to wave them away. If more than twelve trosips attack one victim, both of two saving throws must succeed for the victim to survive.

gm.title: Detection and retreat
lines: A stationary trosip looks like ordinary dust. Magic or devices that detect invisible creatures can reveal it, and some animals such as cats can see it. The colony withdraws once the victim wakes or the body begins cooling. The book describes fast short spurts and poor sustained movement.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Colonies feed on refuse and draw heat from sleepers. One trosip can multiply into 24 or more within a few days. Infants, young children and the infirm are especially vulnerable.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Immune to all effects of the Red Curse.

gm.title: Printing note
lines: The table gives Tiny size and prints a 6′–9′ diameter. Both figures are kept because the book gives no corrected measurement.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Keensense lets the creature perceive its surroundings without relying on sight.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A burrowing relative of the giant centipede at least 25 feet long, with powerful mandibles.

gm.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Burrow lunge · A lunge from its hidden burrow gets +2 to hit. A hit seizes the target in its mandibles. The lunge causes no damage until it chews through the armor.

Armor breach · Leather or worse takes one round. Armor tougher than leather through chain mail takes two. Armor tougher than chain mail takes three. Once the armor is breached, the worm deals 2d8 damage automatically each round.
Retreat · It releases the victim and retreats to its lair after taking at least 15 points of fire damage or losing 60% of its HP.

gm.title: Lair mechanics
lines: Carrion and treasure · It eats carrion, lays eggs in it, and may leave treasure from former victims in its lair.

gm.title: Appearance notes mechanics
lines: Body plan · The segmented body and short walking legs depict its stated kinship with centipedes. The book does not specify a palette for this form.

gm.title: Table notes

lines: A bite has a 5% chance to transmit a serious disease unless the victim saves vs. poison. The entry gives examples of disease but no onset, duration or further damage.

gm.title: Red Curse

gm.title: Phase Legacy
lines: If the voat has Phase, it can pass through solid matter for 1 round, up to three times daily once the Legacy is fully active. It can walk without sinking during deliberate phasing. The full effect is immune to solid weapons while phased, but magic missile, the Missile Legacy and magical fire, cold and electricity can still affect it. The Affliction and active Legacy are separate effects.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Packs raid granaries and ship cargo, gnaw through planks, and foul what they leave. They also nest in caves containing scarlet pimpernels. Nests may hold bright objects and gear from victims. Voats live 2–4 years and typically have 3–5 litters a year of 8–12. Cardinal ticks often infest them, and packs sometimes associate with Saragón lyra birds.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Printed source

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Carrion Sense. The vulture can pinpoint by scent any carrion, dead creature, or undead without Incorporeal Movement within 60 ft. of it.
Heightened Sight and Smell. The vulture's Perception is 18 when using sight or smell.
Pack Tactics. The vulture has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one ally of the vulture is within 5 ft. of the creature and that ally is not incapacitated.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Beak attack and one Talons attack.
Beak. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Talons. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Defensive Bile. When a creature the vulture can see hits it with a melee attack from within 5 ft., the vulture can spit partially digested carrion at the attacker. On a failed DC 13 Constitution save, the attacker takes 5 (2d4) acid damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: Roll 2d8 HP per adult under the Appendix Hit Dice rule. Pups use 1d4 HP.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A long-haired grey hound with a bare reddish vulture head, hooked beak, small feathered wings and curved talons.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: 4d6 appearing. Rare. Day-active carnivore. Pack. Animal intelligence (1). Treasure J (×10), K (×10), L (×5), M, N. Average morale (8–10). No magic resistance or listed special defenses.

gm.title: Printed source
lines:
TSR, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix (1996), pp. 117–118. 
Additional rule references: Appendix pp. 4, 6–8 and Savage Coast Campaign Book Part 2 pp. 85, 96 and 104 for Class C flight and Legacy procedures.

gm.title: Combat
lines: When it can rear up, the vulturehound makes three attacks: two front talons for 1d3 each and one beak for 1d4. If it cannot rear, use the beak alone. In flight, it attacks with its front talons. It loses flight after losing more than 75% of starting HP. At exactly 75% loss, it can still fly. Class C movement requires at least half speed, allows a 90-degree turn per round and permits an aerial attack pass every two rounds.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Renardy packs acquire Legacies but never suffer Affliction. Yazak Steppes populations lie outside the Red Curse’s direct influence. The text lists Gas Breath, Acid Touch, Gaseous Form and Sleep as common choices. Assign the individual’s Legacy before play.

gm.title: Common Legacies
lines: A fully active Legacy has up to three uses per day. Use the adult’s 2 HD as caster level. Gas Breath lasts up to 2 rounds before expiring and delivers one 1d4 poison hit to a target within 5 ft. Magical poison protection can grant a save vs. poison for half. Acid Touch is instantaneous and deals 1d4 + 2 on a successful hit against plant matter or flesh. Gaseous Form lasts 2 rounds with flight 3 (B), can pass through gaps that are not airtight, and can be driven by normal or magical winds. Most attacks cannot affect it. Magical fire, electricity, magic missile and the Missile Legacy can. Sleep lasts 4 rounds, targets one living creature closest to a location within 10 yards, and allows a save vs. spell.

gm.title: Pack and pups
lines: Packs hunt out of a den and drag back food. Their lair has a 50% chance to hold 3d4 pups. A pup has 1d4 HP, cannot fly, and bites for 1d2 damage. Pups taken young can be trained for war or hunting. A trained adult tracks as a 5th-level ranger or adds +3 to a ranger companion’s tracking skill. Each vulturehound has a 50% chance of cardinal ticks.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Vulturehounds take carrion and hunt isolated or sick prey. They watch and scent for carrion and bay like dogs. They are immune to vermilia. One animal yields enough blood for 1d6 doses of antivermilia medicine, made by a mage of at least 9th level with an alchemical laboratory. A dose cures a man-sized or smaller creature. The book says doses often cost over 150 gp.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An enormous sea reptile with an eel-like body and a long, lashing tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Hold Breath. The wakewyrm can hold its breath for 1 hour.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack, or two Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit for 15 (3d6 + 5) piercing damage. On a failed DC 16 Strength save, the target is Grappled (escape DC 16). While grappling a creature, the wakewyrm cannot grapple a second creature or Bite a different target.
Tail. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 25 ft., one target. Hit for 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack against a Large or smaller creature the wakewyrm is grappling. On a hit, the grapple ends and the target is swallowed. It is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects outside the wakewyrm, and takes 11 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the wakewyrm’s turns. If a creature inside deals at least 18 damage to the wakewyrm, the wakewyrm must make a DC 15 Constitution save at the end of that creature’s turn. On a failure, the wakewyrm disgorges every swallowed creature, and each falls Prone in a space within 10 ft. If the wakewyrm dies, swallowed creatures are no longer Restrained by it and can spend 20 ft. of movement to escape. Its body floats for several hours before gradually sinking.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A stout single-humped camel with a strong neck and heavy shoulders.

gm.title: Special attacks mechanics
lines: Spitting · An ill-tempered camel has a 50% chance to spit at someone who tries to ride it or use it as a pack animal. The victim then has a 25% chance of being blinded for 1–3 rounds.

Herd stampede · A frightened herd has a 25% chance of stampeding. Roll 2d4 camels for each creature in its path that fails to take cover. Each camel deals 1–4 damage to that creature. Trampled creatures stay down until the herd passes.
Bite and hooves · The war camel bites for 1d4 and attacks twice with its hooves for 1d6 each. A successful hoof attack keeps the opponent prone.

gm.title: Handling mechanics
lines: Carrying capacity · Load by weight in gold pieces: 200 normal, 300 encumbered, 400 fully encumbered. Camels kneel to be loaded and often refuse to rise with more than their encumbered load.
War camel use · Often trained for years from the strongest desert camels, or selectively bred from retired war camels.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: 1–12 appearing. Elite (13) morale. Animal to semi-intelligent (1–4).
Common, diurnal herd herbivore. The table lists any land for terrain and Nil for alignment, treasure, special defenses, and magic resistance.
TSR, Monstrous Compendium Al-Qadim Appendix (1992), unnumbered Camel leaf (p. 11).

lines: Two Hooves +3 melee for 1d3 + 2 damage each.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Environment. Temperate plains. Organization. Domesticated. War ponies are bred to fight while mounted and resemble light warhorses. Treasure none. Advancement. None listed. Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Mounted combat
lines: The pony can fight while carrying a rider. For the rider to attack as well, use the war-trained mount Ride check, DC 10 as a free action.

gm.title: Carrying capacity
lines: Light load up to 100 lb. Medium load 101–200 lb. Heavy load 201–300 lb. Drag limit 1,500 lb.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An enormous eight-legged spider with blade-edged legs and a broad back that can carry a goblin archery platform.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Bite · melee · +6 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 2d6 + 4 piercing plus 2d6 poison
Bladed Leg · melee · +6 to hit · reach 10 ft. · 2d6 + 4 slashing

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Baby Burst · At death, release one Swarm of Insects (spiders). It acts on the War Spider’s initiative count.

Rider Launcher · An allied rider jumping off the spider can long jump 30 ft. or high jump 15 ft. from a standstill or running start. The rider has advantage on its first melee weapon attack that turn.
Spider Climb · The spider can climb difficult surfaces and traverse ceilings without a check.
Web Walker · Webbing does not restrict the spider’s movement.
Wide Back · Two Small or Tiny riders can share a space on the spider. It carries up to 18 Small or 64 Tiny riders.

gm.title: Action mechanics
lines: Web Spray · Each creature in a 15-ft. cube must make a DC 13 Dexterity save or be restrained. A creature can use an action to attempt a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity check, freeing itself or a creature within its reach on a success.

Trample (Recharge 6) · Move up to its speed through other creatures’ spaces. Make one Bladed Leg attack against each creature whose space the spider enters. A hit removes that creature’s reactions until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: MCDM, Flee, Mortals! public preview, pp. 5 and 9. Unaligned. Proficiency bonus +2. No languages.
The Goblins chapter places outlaw goblin encounters in deserts, forests, and underground. The preview gives no separate natural habitat for this beast.
Goblins use the spider as a battle mount, with archers above and riders that jump into melee. Use Web Spray to hold a group in place or Trample to move through an enemy line.

lines:

gm.title: Optional Wildcat Features
lines:
Adept Climber (clouded leopard, jaguar, leopard, lynx, or snow leopard). Gain a climb speed of 25 ft.
Agile Landing (any Medium wildcat). Ignore falls of 40 ft. or less unless Incapacitated.
Deadly Bite (lion, tiger, or jaguar). A Bite hit against a Prone target is a critical hit.
Desert Dweller (sand cat). Ignore difficult terrain from dirt or sand and tolerate temperatures up to 120°F. Fresh food meets the cat's need for water.
Mountain Dweller (lynx or snow leopard). Ignore difficult terrain from snow, ice, or steep slopes.
Superior Sprint (cheetah or sand cat, 2 uses per short or long rest). When the cat moves on its turn in combat, it can quadruple its speed until the turn ends. Replaces Sprint.
Pack Tactics (lion). The cat has advantage on attacks against a target within 5 ft. of at least one ally of the cat, as long as the ally is not Incapacitated.
Powerful Leap (caracal, cougar, lion, margay, serval, or snow leopard). Double all jump distances, with or without a running start. Use either Strength or Dexterity to determine the distance.
Swimmer (tiger, leopard, ocelot, or jaguar). Gain a swim speed of 30 ft.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC is 14 (+2 Dex, +2 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 12. Space/reach 5 ft./5 ft.. Base attack +1. Grapple +2. Fortitude +5, Reflex +5, Will +1.

lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Wolf. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/wolf.htm

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.
With Track, a fresh scent trail typically starts at Survival DC 10. The DC rises by 2 per hour of age, subject to odor strength and the number of creatures. Surface and visibility modifiers do not apply to scent tracking.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:

Feats. Track (bonus feat), Weapon Focus (bite).

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Environment. Temperate forests. Organization. Solitary, pair, or pack (7–16). A pack may engage from the front while others circle to the flanks or rear. Treasure none. Advancement. 3 HD (Medium), 4–6 HD (Large). Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Trip (Ex). When Bite hits, the wolf can try to trip a Large or smaller opponent as a free action. Use its +1 Strength check modifier, opposed by the target’s better Strength or Dexterity modifier, with the normal size and stability adjustments. This needs no touch attack and provokes no attack of opportunity. If it wins, the target falls prone. If it loses, the opponent gets no countertrip.

gm.title: Combat
lines: One ordinary bite for 1d3 damage. The wynzet usually allows petting and feeding. It wins a forest despoiler’s trust before launching its special throat bite.

gm.title: Bite Legacy
lines: Once it has befriended a despoiler, it can leap up to 15 ft. for the throat attack at +4 to hit. On the first successful attack, the target saves vs. paralyzation with Dexterity bonuses. Failure kills the target. Success still deals 2d8 damage. Later attacks deal 1d8 with the active Legacy or 1d3 with the ordinary bite.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: All wynzets have the Bite Legacy and require no cinnabryl. The general Bite Legacy lasts 1 round per level. At 1 HD the duration is 1 round, up to three activations daily when fully active. The entry specifies the special first hit and does not give a separate reset trigger.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Robrenn’s druids empower these woodland guardians. They breed as the creature they resemble, and about 5% of their offspring are wynzets. A despoiler’s remains replenish the forest. In Renardy the beast is sometimes called le lapin mortel.

Flyby Attack. Melee, standard, at-will. Fly up to 8 squares and make one melee basic attack at any point during the movement. It provokes no opportunity attacks while moving away from the target of that attack.

gm.title: Mount
lines: Aerial Agility +2, at-will, Mount. While the wyvern is flying with a rider of level 10 or higher, that rider gains +2 to all defenses.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: All three wyverns fly over the Old Troll Wall. They go after the adventurers once the adventurers attack. They use Claws from the air and land to help the other attackers if those allies are engaged in melee, alternating Bite and Sting. The troglodyte remounts a wyvern if its manticore is killed first.

printings.label: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A fifteen-foot-tall tortoise with a high dome of overlapping shell plates, a thick beaked head, and sturdy legs.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. Understands Goblin but cannot speak.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Chapter 1, A Fateful Competition, J6 Herding the Horizonbacks, p. 26. Use the Ankylosaurus base block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 79. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/a-fateful-competition#AdventureStart

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The tortoise can breathe air and water.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, 10 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 18 (4d6 + 4) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.

gm.title: Base-block action
lines: The inherited Ankylosaurus Tail is a +7 melee weapon attack with 10 ft. reach against one target. It deals 18 (4d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Jigow’s young horizonbacks move from a paddock to fields west of the Jumble, where they start training as mounts and mobile buildings.

gm.title: Encounter application
lines: Maneuvering a tortoise takes three successful Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks, starting at DC 12 and increasing by 1 after each check. On a failed check, it bucks the rider, who must make a DC 13 Dexterity save or fall for 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. Remounting requires a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. Failure prompts a Bite. A tortoise charmed through animal friendship or a similar effect does not buck its handler on a failed check, and the handler has advantage on checks to guide it.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The printed variant gives the tortoise a Bite modeled on the 2014 Ankylosaurus Tail. The adventure describes use of Bite and never expressly removes Tail. The indexed summary presents Bite alone. The Huge Beast classification comes from the parent block.

gm.title: Source hold
lines: Collected Appendix A, v.18 or matching licensed edition

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A juvenile eel-like sea reptile with side fins and small spines along its back.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Bite · Melee Weapon Attack · +5 to hit · reach 10 ft. · 2d6 + 3 piercing

gm.title: Traits mechanics
lines: Hold Breath · Can hold its breath for 1 hour.

gm.title: Bonus Actions mechanics
lines: Plaintive Cry · The juvenile calls for its mother. If she is within 150 ft. and can hear it, she can use her reaction to move up to her speed toward the juvenile.

gm.title: Actions mechanics
lines: Multiattack · 2 attacks · The juvenile makes two Bite attacks.
Bite · +5 to hit · reach 10 ft. · One creature takes 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage on a hit. · 2d6 + 3 piercing

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The adventure shows the juvenile swimming in Tideswell Cave. The card prints one speed of 30 ft. without a separate swim speed.
In the Wakewyrm’s Pool encounter, a DC 16 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check calms the juvenile. It lashes out at creatures in bite range if they fail to calm it. See adventure booklet p. 8.
Hit Point Press, The Wakewyrm's Fury, Reference Cards, p. 5.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A half-grown wolf with a dense snow-white coat, a bushy tail and pale blue eyes.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC includes natural armor. Languages none.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Tales from the Yawning Portal, April 2017 first printing, p. 181, Against the Giants, Glacial Rift upper level, area 4, Small Ice Cave. Base rules from Monster Manual (2014), Dire Wolf, p. 321.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Keen Hearing and Smell. The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Pack Tactics. The wolf has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if one of its allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and is not incapacitated.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage. A creature hit this way falls prone on a failed DC 13 Strength save.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: Three half-grown pups share a bone-strewn cave with two adult winter wolves. If the pups are harmed, the adults accept the risk of opportunity attacks and group up to kill quickly.

gm.title: Description
lines: Cave traders prize these sweet tunnel moth larvae for the burst of strength they give anyone who eats one alive.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Darkvision 30 ft., passive Perception 8. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Death Wail. When the yumgrub dies, creatures within 15 ft. that hear it take 1 psychic damage. Other yumgrubs and anyone who ate one within the past minute are immune.
Spider Climb. Climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Yum. A Small or larger creature can spend an action to eat a living yumgrub within 5 ft. The yumgrub dies. For 1 minute the eater doubles its speed and gains +4 to Strength and +2 to AC. When the minute ends, the eater gains two levels of Exhaustion.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite (group attack). Melee weapon attack, −1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1 piercing damage per participant.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A compact equine with black and pale stripes, a short upright mane, rounded ears and a thin tufted tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Passive Perception 10. No listed languages or special senses.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Tomb of Annihilation, First printing, September 2017, printed p. 106, p. 107. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/toa/dwellers-of-the-forbidden-city Uses Riding Horse, Monster Manual (2014), printed p. 336. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16997-riding-horse

gm.title: Actions
lines: Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Wongo’s Shrine gives the Zebra the Riding Horse statistics. When the shrine masks deliver their curse, anyone who looked through one in the last hour makes a DC 15 Constitution save. A failed save transforms the viewer into the animal on the last mask they used, as polymorph. The curse ends after 24 hours.

gm.title: Base-stat erratum
lines: First-print Monster Manual p. 336 gives Hooves +2 to hit for the Riding Horse. The official errata had corrected it to +5 by 2016. The 2017 Zebra reference uses the corrected Riding Horse block.

name: A bag with a forwarding address

gm.title: At the table
lines: Objects put in a bag appear in a former owner's washbasin. The washbasin keeper has begun labeling and selling the arrivals.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Grain runs short before winter. A retired ovensweeper who buys kiln ash to repair old mortar remembers bricking up the municipal grain store behind a bake oven. They will show the party where if the city promises to pay for the repairs.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An honest ally switches sides when an enemy buys their debt. Make their change of allegiance negotiable and let the party learn the terms.

name: A bargain with nobody left to collect

gm.title: At the table
lines: A villain keeps a borrowed talent until the other party receives the agreed payment. Find the lawful successor and ask whether they want the bargain fulfilled or renegotiated.

name: A basket full of unripe berries

gm.title: At the table
lines: Foragers are stripping a patch before its fruit is ready. Their village expects a hard frost and needs news from the weather tower.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The same light is an invitation on the way out and a distress call on the way back. A lighthouse keeper will share the signal book if the party helps repair the boat that takes them off shift.

name: A bell auction chooses who rings the thaw

gm.title: At the table
lines: The winning bidder rings in spring. Any fishing boat within earshot can launch that day without paying. The old bell has cracked and the new one can be heard from the disputed island, where the regular fee is still contested. Players can help decide whether to move it, repair the old bell, or require two signals.

name: A bellows draws in the marsh

gm.title: At the table
lines: One room smells of peat when a forge operates even though every chimney exits uphill. Pull the bellows when the forge is cold. Wet reeds catch on its intake grate. Behind the grate a broad duct descends to a flooded passage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wild boar uproots a strip of plants while ignoring all the others. A forager demonstrates how it is following a buried edible root.

name: A bone key leaves a debt

gm.title: At the table
