lines: A match lights only while submerged. Ask who installed a candle bracket below the old mill's waterline.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker's skin turns brassy and blunts the first puncture. A visible dent shows where the protection spent itself.

name: Mileage stones count toward a vanished gate

gm.title: At the table
lines: The stones agree with each other and disagree with the modern map. Trace their longest straight run to find a buried toll gate and a route the modern patrols ignore.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Roadside jobseekers can imitate the sound of any hawker they heard. The party can trade an introduction for a demonstration of the last cry.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Blue mold spoils only pages written with one ink. Reconstruct the missing amounts from the buyers' sealed copies.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two armed travelers on their wedding trip ask for a scenic excursion. One wants an audience and another wants a place that gives them privacy.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A storm presses birds, merchants, and guests into the same covered market. The drain beneath their shelter is blocked with snapped spars.

name: Offer a decision tied to a stated ideal

gm.title: At the table
lines: Pick a belief a player has already shown in play. Give the opposition a proposal that honors the belief at a cost. Leave who pays and how the character responds open.

name: Offer the same clue through an action of another kind

gm.title: At the table
lines: Assign one clue to two approaches with different costs. Watching a crew may take an hour, while helping them lifts the delay but exposes the helper to questions. If the group has already learned the fact, reward the second approach with context instead of repeating the clue.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker may disappear and reappear a few steps away once. The destination must be visible at the start of the move.

name: One missing pane makes a visible opening

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lead lines in a window unfold into a guardian at closing. A color added during a different restoration is stiff at the joints. Bring the pane its maker kept as a sample to close the gap, or pass through while guarding that weak spot against another visitor.

gm.title: At the table
lines: At the start of a round, a swarm divides its existing mass between two objectives. Ringing a bell draws the nearest group toward it. Joining bodies restores reach at the cost of covering less ground.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Identify where a person stopped seeing the events you mapped. Let them distinguish what they witnessed from the claim someone paid them to repeat.

name: One wooden joint has no pin

gm.title: At the table
lines: A model of an automaton moves a leg that has no physical joint. Check the larger machine for empty space where a drive pin ought to be.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A small marsh spirit trims lamps along the safest causeway. When a new keeper moves the lamps, it follows the old route anyway and can show the party which stakes were moved.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every clap releases colored scraps. Their landing points help mark a floor the party has to cross more than once.

name: Pay off a thing the players chose to keep

gm.title: At the table
lines: Pick an object or contact they saved at an earlier cost. Offer a contribution available because it survived and let the players decide whether to use it now or save it again.

name: Pay the host in tomorrow's help

gm.title: At the table
lines: An innkeeper will waive a charge in exchange for public help with one concrete job before noon. Name the job and an alternative before the party agrees. The host provides the tools while the players decide how visible their involvement should be.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tiny scene in a pendant spins whenever a particular threshold is open. Compare its spin against a clock to find the next window.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ritualist keeps redrawing a ward whose flawed version would hold long enough. Ask the players which flaw they accept.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ask what the attacker wants from the people they are fighting. Put an object or witness in the space that can still prove that goal was met.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A few townspeople turn to stone with one hand extended. They had all tried to stop the same fairground machine.

name: Pick one person the character could ask for shelter

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ask what that person needs to see before opening the door today. Write their answer down with a smaller favor they could still give if the shelter is unavailable.

name: Picks that refuse a closed lock

gm.title: At the table
lines: A set of picks will turn the bolt only while the latch is open. A watch officer asks the party to find the owner who used it to lock a door from the outside.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A group sets out without dry clothing for its final climb. The leader refuses new gear unless it is freely offered under their rules.

name: Plates that record a shared meal

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each cracked plate breaks after serving one guest. The glaze exposes an identifying mark when it fractures.

name: Play the person behind the encounter

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the gate guard an overdue errand. Players can solve that problem and change what the guard is willing to do.

name: Plot the aftermath at three time scales

gm.title: At the table
lines: Before a major choice, write changes the party could see by nightfall, hear about a week later, and deal with next season. Tie each to a different person with the ability to act. Move only the consequences supported by what actually happened.

gm.title: At the table
lines: This long-legged burrower issues a soft knock when someone stands directly over its nest, then shoves loose boards upward if they linger. Its young leave sweep marks under the threshold. Laying a solid plank across both supports lets visitors pass while the animals keep the porch.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Festival portraits walk out of their frames and attempt the job their subject wished to abandon. One has already signed a binding contract.

name: Prepare the adversary's explanation after a setback

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write what the opponent tells their own followers if the party interrupts the plan. Make the explanation testable through one visible lie or omission. Players who expose it can change what the followers will do next, even when the opponent escapes.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write one action per active group and when it will happen. If players spend time elsewhere, advance only the actions still possible. Bring up traces the party can observe before its next decision and strike out actions overtaken by play.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A watch captain refuses outside help until the party gives them a way to warn the town without losing command.

name: Protect something people can work on

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the party a fragile asset whose location and state they can always see. Add ways for players to relocate it, repair it, or ask for cover when they need an extra minute.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An uncommon bird is nesting on an old marker. One collector wants its feathers and one historian wants the lettering beneath the nest.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Extortionists issue stamped receipts. A merchant has two with different embossing for the same shop.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fiend assigned to a road offers an escort as far as its last milepost. Someone has been moving that post to claim protection for a different road.

gm.title: At the table
lines: When players enjoy opening negotiations, give an opponent something they can offer or withdraw in public. Have the response change who outside the scene becomes invested.

name: Put a final choice after the last confrontation

gm.title: At the table
lines: Let the decisive confrontation answer whether the party gains control of something. Give them a more intimate choice afterward about how to return, share, or retire it. Name the people each option affects before the confrontation starts.

name: Put an alibi at two observation distances

gm.title: At the table
lines: One witness recognizes a distinctive garment from far away. Another can distinguish the wearer's voice at close range. Sketch where they stood and let the party decide whether both observations refer to the same person.

name: Put the weather on a path

gm.title: At the table
lines: Start with clear skies, then put gusts and rain on a path in that order. At the end of a watch roll a die: odd holds the condition, even moves to the next one, and the rain leads back to clear skies. The guide knows gusts foreshadow rain and thinning cloud means an end to it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sick district closes to traffic and unpaid porters refuse to unload supplies outside it. A carrier has a plausible plan if someone covers their lost wages.

name: Raiders keep an account of guard shifts

gm.title: At the table
lines: A band watches the road and writes down every patrol. They are documenting missing guards to sell the record back to the watch.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A group returning from a raid sells tools below their cost. Their guide is prepared to show where the tools came from if someone pays wages owed.

name: Rain makes a chalk slope readable

gm.title: At the table
lines: Dark mineral lines appear during rain and indicate where previous travelers carved steps under the moss. Waiting for another shower costs daylight. A surveyor can learn the route by drawing the lines before they fade.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker smells of approaching rain. Animals settle before an actual storm and stir again when they notice the false smell.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Unusually bold rats carry bundles between sewer grates. One bundle falls open and contains copies of a baker's lease.

name: Read the stall signs before splitting up

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give players two paths and name a visible trade on each. Choose an obstacle produced by its everyday work, such as a basket washer's wet passage versus a fruit cart's crowded corner. Let players anticipate one effect before committing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: During a break, let players post a job with a specific duration and a wage. In the morning offer two applicants with different means or local relationships and let the party pick whom to trust.

gm.title: At the table
lines: For an hour reflections lag the drinker's movements. An observer can test which window is glass and which is a patient illusion.

name: Reopen a quiet scene with a question from the fiction

gm.title: At the table
lines: If the table stalls, have someone in the scene ask a question whose answer must change their next action. A porter can ask which passenger boards before the crossing closes. Use the answer to move the scene even if no one reaches for a die.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A child stuck in a well insists that their friend comes up first. The friend is moving in a side tunnel below the waterline.

name: Reserve an epilogue for the people who stayed

gm.title: At the table
lines: After the immediate crisis, show one recurring local or institution coping with the outcome a week later. Invite each player to contribute a change their character helped make happen. Preserve the part of the decision the group still disagrees about.

name: Reunited marks change the next appointment

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two members of a bargain have a standing time to reconcile a debt. Bringing their marks together while each agrees to meet shifts the next appointment one day. The new ink is visible to both and neither can move it further until they keep that meeting.

name: Reuse a question at the point the answer costs more

gm.title: At the table
lines: An earlier scene asks for a consequence-free opinion. Later a person can act on that opinion and someone will bear the cost. Begin by reminding the group who heard the earlier answer before giving them the new option.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the opposition a place with a secret worth discovering even if the party never confronts them. Make exploring it change which routes, allies, or tools the party has.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Customers play their way through locked rooms. A regular has learned to leave one door unlatched during each round.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The eel wedges its plated head beneath moving metal and waits for the vibration to stop. A stopped mechanism and a bent rivet warn of its presence. Players can ease it out by slowly turning a spare gear, draw it to another machine, or repair the mechanism after lifting it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An artist repaints each guest room when a visitor checks out. A previous resident left clues only in the unfinished border of the paint.

name: Run the villain's adventure before yours

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write what the opposition attempted in three short beats before the party arrived. Give each beat a trace that an ordinary person could still find.

name: Salvage floats over a feeding ground

gm.title: At the table
lines: The turtle that sank a merchant convoy now waits under the salvage site. Three captains are trading false dive times to send rivals down first. Spot which marked buoy the turtle avoids before choosing whether to dive or negotiate.

name: Scope a curse with something cheap

gm.title: At the table
lines: Before asking players to risk a character or prized possession, show a cheap object affected at one boundary and untouched at another. The party can identify one rule reliably before dealing with an exception.

name: Separate a shared project from its incompatible motives

gm.title: At the table
lines: Both allies want the same repair. One needs open passage by dawn, and the other wants the restoration record to prove prior ownership. Describe one solution that satisfies only each ally and a costlier one that satisfies both.

name: Settlers choose between water and land

gm.title: At the table
lines: New arrivals can settle the only clean spring or the only field ready to sow. Existing residents can offer a third site if their boundary dispute is resolved.

gm.title: At the table
lines: At midnight neglected shadows refuse to follow their owners. A shuttered square offers the only shelter and its keeper wants a promise before opening it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The proprietor serves fugitives under a strict peace. The watch asks the party to identify a customer without breaking that custom.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hag displays a cabinet of victims' shoes. One pair is still muddy from a trail that she says has been closed for years.

name: Show a reliable forecast before the last decision

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write one consequence each faction could deduce from facts they already know before the climax. Let each disclose it through a different witness. When one forecast comes true, the witnesses can revisit promises they made in advance.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Put flood marks over the lower door before the tide comes in. Players can act on the hazard before risking a roll.

name: Show what a victory frees someone to do

gm.title: At the table
lines: Pick someone who spent several sessions maintaining a defense or obligation. Once the characters succeed, offer a short scene in which that person can stop, spend the time elsewhere, or decide the role still matters to them.

name: Show what changed since the outward trip

gm.title: At the table
lines: On a return leg, repeat one landmark and show how a previous choice affected it. Give it a practical consequence such as a new river crossing, a safe place to rest, or visitors asking who repaired the bridge.

name: Signal the next consequence in plain language

gm.title: At the table
lines: If a dangerous detail has escaped notice, summarize what the characters can already see and what will happen if no one acts. Ask for a choice before calling for a roll. Use this when an avoidable setback would otherwise come from a misunderstanding of the scene.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The moths build translucent nests in door gaps where temperature stays steady. Moving the door swings the whole colony into a room and briefly clouds nearby lamps. Their nests can be lifted intact by warming the opposite sill, so discovery need not become a fight.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Skeletons repair a road while a priest supervises. The priest is willing to leave if the party will get the townsfolk to perform the necessary work.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The cook can recognize every dish they made in life. A funeral recipe brings the staff out to ask who taught the customer to make it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Several lights chase one another over the hills. A settled fire spot below one of the crossings contains tracks in opposite directions.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker gets narrow pupils that help them pick a face out in glare. It is obvious to anyone standing opposite.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A single harmless cough makes a smoke figure and sends it down the strongest draft. A split in the figure suggests a hidden vent.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A freak snowfall blocks doors at ground level and makes windows reachable. A storekeeper asks the party to escort volunteers down a new route.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bar leaves a distinct bad smell that locals associate with a ruined bathhouse. Offer a public demonstration before an accusation based on smell goes further.

name: Somebody on the wagon needs to get off safely

gm.title: At the table
lines: The target is a cart whose driver is leaving to avoid an inquiry. An apprentice inside wants to dismount without being injured. Give one safe transfer point and one uncertain chance to stop the cart before it reaches it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An excited crowd points toward a healer outside the wall. A cart driver can show the party where the accuser bought their proof.

name: Someone files for credit before the job ends

gm.title: At the table
lines: The guild pays a bonus to the first named crew that completes a rescue. A second party files a claim while missing people are still unaccounted for. Players can ask a clerk to postpone the award, negotiate shared credit, or get the outstanding names read into the record.

name: Someone in the trap won't shout

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trapped stranger asks for silence before rescue. The trapper is nearby and waiting for the sound of their own missing pet.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Cheap charms lose their magic in the order they were sold. The maker kept receipt numbers inside each clasp.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The tern unspools lengths of fiber from unattended gear to tie a nest above the flood line. A ribbon fluttering upstream shows where it has worked. Offer loose cord to recover a marked piece of evidence or follow the new nest before the next tide.

name: Squid ink sits in bands along the silty wall

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hunter's passing leaves a pale clearance between older ink bands. The bands tell which overhang a squid has stopped using. Fresh broken shells under a second overhang put the squid there recently. New drag marks leading away from the first shelter show something also disturbed it.

name: Start where a choice is available

gm.title: At the table
lines: Show what has already changed and one thing the party can do today. Keep additional history within reach of players who want it after they choose an approach.

name: Start with what will be hard to move

gm.title: At the table
lines: Sketch the festival around one object or act that needs space, time, or skilled hands. Ask who can move it, who is forbidden to, and one thing that goes wrong if it arrives an hour late.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Hair rises around the drinker. It leans farther in a room with a charged object nearby.

name: Stop an object leaving the scene

gm.title: At the table
lines: Name the gate, cart, or portal through which a courier plans to leave with the object. Let the party intercept what matters by checking exits as well as confronting the courier.

name: Straps made from the wrong leather

gm.title: At the table
lines: A pack strap splits along a hidden repair. A trader can replace it but asks to see the original receipt before selling to the group.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hole opens under a stall. Looking sideways into it shows colored windows beneath the street.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Chalk letters migrate between walls following changes in the wind. Catch them around three corners to reconstruct a stolen warning.

name: Strength until the minute hand moves

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker can hold a heavy load for a short time. Set a visible clock before asking who will take the weight next.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old guide trusts a trail that was safe before a landslide. Let the party spot new survey stakes and decide how to get the guide to look.

name: Swap the viewpoint on a piece of evidence

gm.title: At the table
lines: Introduce a record for a concrete purpose in one thread. Later put it in reach of a different contact who can interpret a secondary mark or omission. Keep both readings true so the players retain the value of their earlier conclusion.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bracelet has a different number cut into each bead. The local ferryman issues the same numbers as tickets.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Ruined farm terraces have no visible approach. Looking at them from across the valley shows where the old stair towers were.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wrapped baby is left at the edge of a trail with a marker showing where to find shelter. No tracks lead back the way the party came.

name: The abandoned meal was prepared for a left hand

gm.title: At the table
lines: At a place setting, the knife lies to the left and the mug handle faces the door. Give a witness who sets every place that way and a pantry tally that identifies the meal's actual recipient. Let the sight of the table suggest a lead without making handedness prove identity.

name: The acorn on a loose board

gm.title: At the table
lines: A carved plank was cut from a door with a distinctive width. The wood under the acorn stayed dry through a fire that burned the rest.

name: The alarm line has an honest repair knot

gm.title: At the table
lines: A visible cord connects bells across two rooms. A fresh knot marks a repair that can be untied without setting it off, but opening that connection leaves a third room without its promised warning. Let the party brief the people there or decide they have time to fix the line afterward.

name: The archive creature gives up a floor at closing

gm.title: At the table
lines: The upper shelves slowly fold inward while shoppers still browse downstairs. A worker can prop one section with a shelf label from the same year. Ask the creature which section it will close last in exchange for help moving people out.

name: The ball knows an old league

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ball runs drills on a sand court all by itself. Its route outlines positions required for a game the town banned.

name: The baths close the wrong locker

gm.title: At the table
lines: The attendant has instructions to seal one numbered locker. Both rooms have a locker with that number. The key log shows the attendant started with the right locker, but the drying-rack assignments were swapped ten minutes before closing. The worker who signed the swap can say who requested it.

name: The battle with a missing beat

gm.title: At the table
lines: The amphitheater replays an old battle after sunset. One sound in the middle goes missing whenever a particular visitor approaches.

name: The bell was muffled between strikes

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wake bell should have rung twice, but the lantern keeper saw only one flash from the belfry. Show wax on the clapper and a watch log that distinguishes a silent second strike from a missed signal. Whoever muffled it may have been trying to keep mourners from gathering on an unsafe stair.

name: The bilge cat finds a quiet place that moves

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shy animal hides the instant the ship changes sides in a rolling swell. The hiding place is in a hammock wedged behind a cargo stack. Give it somewhere else to shelter and follow its old route to the loose fastenings.

name: The bird-watching blind faces the wrong way

gm.title: At the table
lines: The creek birds gather behind the blind. Whoever built it meant to watch which wagons stopped at a barn on the hill. Old perch holes provide clear viewing angles and show how much of the road they could actually see.

name: The boundary stones cast new shadows

gm.title: At the table
lines: Standing stones seem to point to a new location at dawn. Checking the bases reveals which stones were turned.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each hour the building shakes and mugs slide into grooves. One table has fresh braces and somebody keeps pointing it toward the cellar door.

name: The burrow opens into a mill pond

gm.title: At the table
lines: A digging creature sleeps downstream from the wheel and leaves when the pond drops. A miller's chalk marks show how long the water takes to reach its den. The party can lower the pond, find the cause of the blockage, and restore the water before the miller's next delivery.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Stone cairns point the same way except for one. Its odd alignment was designed to guide mourners when standing water covers the usual path.

name: The captain's sealed cabin is a transit room

gm.title: At the table
lines: A concealed cabin has a chalk circle and its door is locked from the hall. The ship's old charts give three ports where a matching circle could receive the next passenger.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stone giant brings a train of loaded elephants but the town's ramp has collapsed. Hire locals to make a new unloading point before rain.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A battered caravan arrives with full barrels despite losing its draft teams. Ask what the drivers traded for the strength to push them uphill.

name: The carrier charges by shelf space

gm.title: At the table
lines: A merchant can deliver heavy stock, but the fee depends on stack height rather than weight. Give the party an option to pack it themselves, wait for another order that shares a shelf, or collect one of their larger parcels at the shop before the carrier loads it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A ball of yarn summons the nearest cat. One regular arrival wears a paper tag describing an inaccessible room.

name: The ceiling goes quiet when barred

gm.title: At the table
lines: An overhead chain rattles while a hidden sluice is open, warning that water is flowing over an otherwise fordable passage. One group can hold the gate closed from its control room while the other crosses on the quiet signal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Gravity pulls toward different walls in different rooms. A room key dropped from the balcony lands on a ceiling tile with a name written underneath.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wrestler has agreed to lose for money and realizes their supposed opponent has disappeared. They ask for a stand-in with a different plan.

name: The chapel above a breath of air

gm.title: At the table
lines: A submerged monastery keeps one dry guest hall. When storms approach, the hall's air is shared with neighboring divers and somebody has to make the guest list.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A major temple closes between services. Choristers inside signal that they can still attend to the sick if the side gate opens.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The creature spends every fourth beat rewinding itself. Telegraphed slowing gives the party a chance to block the key or bargain with its attendant.

name: The coat with the dry cuff

gm.title: At the table
lines: A body washes ashore with both cuffs dry but boots full of river silt. The ferryman will identify the clothing if allowed to keep their customer's name private.

name: The common field hosts work and votes on different days

gm.title: At the table
lines: Herder's ropes become polling lines every first day of the month. A delayed sale would leave cattle trampling the ballot approach. Players can move the sale, shift the polling layout, or work out which boundary can handle both uses.

name: The company celebrates a completed job

gm.title: At the table
lines: Mercenaries invite the party to a roadside feast and ask whether their last employer has paid the town. The answer affects whose work they accept.

name: The complaint is about who had to explain the favor

gm.title: At the table
lines: A grateful local is angry because the party publicly paid their debt and left them to explain why. Ask what the local wanted their colleagues to hear first and offer a chance to correct the record together.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Capturing the smuggler ends the deliveries and leaves a village without medicine. Give the party enough information to find an alternate supplier before the shortage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A pigeon circles high above the route with a heavy message tube. It will land on a familiar pattern drawn on a flat roof.

name: The crate overbalances the cargo plan

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crate starts pulling nearby loads toward it during a squall. Check its bill of lading to learn which part of the cargo was supposed to keep it balanced in town.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tavern farms around a fallen stone that hums when touched. Overnight the livestock move to the far edge and the stone rolls a foot in the opposite direction.

name: The crossing collects the wear on your shoes

gm.title: At the table
lines: Walking across a yard reverses the wear on your shoes and transfers it to the floorboards. Careful examination can date a repeated route or show whether someone entered through a door they say they never used.

name: The crypt wraps through its edge

gm.title: At the table
lines: Crossing one inscribed doorway brings you through the opposite edge of the same six-room loop. Give each edge a visible symbol and let thrown chalk reveal the return path before anyone risks crossing.

name: The crystal shows a key from below

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crystal shows the underside of a key. An artisan can identify a distinctive notch and reproduce a harmless blank for checking locks.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cursed blade makes whoever wears it sick. People contest ownership but are eager to have someone else hold it in the meantime.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A missing heir can prove their identity, but title and property have since scattered through good-faith sales. Give the party someone to protect on each side.

name: The deck musician calls a forgotten watch

gm.title: At the table
lines: A drunken navigator repeats verse at odd times. A retired mate recognizes it as instructions once used to shift shifts without passing a written order.

name: The delivery weight includes a passenger

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hoist record shows an empty cradle descending at the weight of a loaded one. Examine wear on the safety strap or find the hook operator's tally before asking who went down. The passenger can be reached by the hoist or by joining the next repair crew.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fey host can name every patron who visited before the inn moved worlds. Half the regulars remember a different town at the last stop.

name: The display model was built to a customer's height

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shop's fitting stand has an old notch with a particular name and date. It used to be adjustable. Find the replacement bracket to establish whether the old measurement belonged to the supposed customer or to a later repair.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An animated rug accepts any guest who wipes their feet or steps around it. Dried marks on the rug show how prior visitors passed. Someone who ignores the request is held long enough for the occupants to ask who sent them.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A dragon passes over town and dips its wing at a hoisted sail. The sailmaker insists someone paid for a pattern they could only see from above.

name: The draught reverses before a flood

gm.title: At the table
lines: Dust on a shelf blows outward while the tunnel drains and inward when water backs up. The change gives the party time to find high ground or divert the next flow, and ribbons offer a cheap way to watch it.

name: The dream bank honors debts that awake people forgot

gm.title: At the table
lines: Farmers leave stamped clay in a night deposit box. At dawn, the numbers appear on the real bank's sealed interest sheet. Ask the dream clerk to read one forgotten debt aloud while a waking clerk checks the amount.

name: The dream theater books a second cast for your promise

gm.title: At the table
lines: At each rehearsal a different actor can play the same role. The role stays bound to a promise the last actor made to a waking person. The players can help cast someone able to keep it or trace the first rehearsal where it was added.

name: The drift boat holds two claims

gm.title: At the table
lines: A skiff carries half of a ship's papers and a dry hammock with a recent stain. One crew wants the papers back and another will identify the person who slept there.

name: The dust keeper tidies only the left half

gm.title: At the table
lines: A house sprite puts small objects away only on the side it was told to clean. A strip of undisturbed dust marks a furniture boundary from long ago. Ask who drew that boundary and what another worker still refuses to clean.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The shell has collapsed inward around a cut on one side. A cry along a fresh drag trail suggests something reached in and removed a live hatchling.

name: The empty chair has an active vote

gm.title: At the table
lines: An absent ogre delegate left written instructions naming whoever brings their favorite dish in the family bowl as proxy. Their deciding vote could reopen a shuttered ferry. Players can fetch the bowl, ask who has been cooking for the delegate, or prove someone struck the dish off the menu.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An abandoned house lights one window for every person who has entered since it closed. Tonight there is one more light than the visitor book accounts for. Send someone inside or call a visitor out to see which light responds.

name: The empty ship sails a shift pattern

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crewless vessel stays on course until it reaches the bend where a missing sailor would have taken the watch. An intact roster gives a rescuer a way to impersonate that sailor long enough to steer.

name: The enemy alone can forgive the breach

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old enemy's sincere forgiveness would break a ruler's protective oath. Treat forgiveness as a decision the enemy can decline even after the party offers restitution.

name: The estate moved a cabinet too wide for the door

gm.title: At the table
lines: The cabinet's dimensions and a dated delivery receipt show it arrived intact after the door was narrowed. A floorplan places an abandoned service stair against the rear wall. Find how the movers opened it to recover the cabinet or enter the estate unnoticed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cartographer refuses to finish one corner because the water carves a fresh channel overnight. Compare their past measurements with a survey at dawn to see where the stream will cut next.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Unattached shadows pool under one market awning. Turn the awning a quarter turn and one shadow still points to the condemned courthouse. The seller will say whose shadow it was if someone agrees to take it down.

gm.title: At the table
lines: This creature reads footfalls instead of faces. It names visitors by their gait and can be misled by carrying someone else across the floor.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Travelers keep asking guests to join their family. At the next checkpoint only caravan members can vouch for each other.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A new society offers lost workers paid tasks. Compare which tasks it puts in writing with the favors it asks from its supporters in person.

name: The feast serves the neighborhood that grew each course

gm.title: At the table
lines: One street supplied mushrooms last year and was left out of the procession when its cellar failed. Its cook is ready to serve a new dish if the festival gives credit publicly. The cellar entrance opens during their allotted course.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Strange feathers hang in an airshaft at the same height. They drop together when the miners open a door three levels below.

name: The first hand becomes the face

gm.title: At the table
lines: A blank doll takes on the face of the first person ever to hold it. Its buyer can check if a supposedly factory-new doll was left for them by someone specific.

name: The fishway has a count that never adds up

gm.title: At the table
lines: The keeper pays to tally fish at both ends of a bypass. Every third fish is recorded at the downstream end but absent upstream. A quieter night watch can catch the creature that carries live fish through a shallow side run.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Tide changes the reach of an anchored dance floor. A deepwater guest can only negotiate during the narrow interval when the deck meets the rocks.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A flash flood cuts between two groups of travelers. One has shelter while the other has the only equipment that can cross.

name: The flooded ledger starts on the wrong side

gm.title: At the table
lines: An archive room flooded from the north, but the wettest edge of a disputed ledger faced the south shelves when it was found. Dry cubby dust and a tray left under a drip can identify its earlier position. The players can use the move to find the hidden shelf or ask who tried to save that book first.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every smith forgets the same step of a sacred craft. An apprentice kept an interrupted practice piece and needs backing to try a different method.

name: The forged contract has an outdated emergency contact

gm.title: At the table
lines: The leaked contract carries a routing mark from one office, but the dispatcher denies stamping it. The emergency contact on the forged copy moved out last year. Find the drawer of old blank contracts and ask who could still get into it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sinkhole swallows the trail while its stone markers drift on water. Those markers are safer footing than the apparently dry fringe.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every basin spout now produces a different potion. Keep an alchemist's results public so the townsfolk can decide which basins to cap.

name: The gate counterweight can hold a person

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jammed freight gate needs more weight to rise. The party can load supplies they may need later, trust an ally to stand in the cradle, or spend time freeing the hand brake. Show the cradle descending toward a runoff channel before anyone climbs inside.

name: The gatekeeper blinks to numbered tiles

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each time the guardian takes a hit it moves to the next intact tile by number. The party can close off tiles, but one of them is also the exit.

name: The glass protector watches only its own reflection

gm.title: At the table
lines: The guardian remains still whenever it sees a full reflection of the window it came from. A tall polished shield can hold it still, or use two mirrors to preserve a line of sight while speaking to the person it was sent to protect.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bilingual dictionary uses extinct river names in all its examples. Someone has written a modern address alongside every translated route.

name: The golem borrows a candle’s remaining length

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wax caretaker extends its forearm with any available stub. Candles on the windows have a different wax formula and leave part of the arm flexible. Offer one to let the golem retrieve something from a narrow duct in exchange for access to the lamp room.

name: The grove asks for an offered path

gm.title: At the table
lines: Druids close a grove to travelers without explaining why. One offers a walkthrough if the group marks paths local animals already take.

name: The guard is on a different job

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stealth scene contains people doing legitimate work. Show what they watch and what sound or movement they routinely ignore.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A merchant asks travelers for stories and one guard takes notes. A phrase from the notes appears on a cheap broadsheet at the next stop.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An ancestral shade appears to only one person per household. Children receive a different warning than the elders and recognize one another's accounts.

name: The guild kit was signed out for a rescue with no address

gm.title: At the table
lines: A dispatcher keeps a duplicate list of kit borrowers. Whoever took several hoists and stretchers left a series of roof spans in place of an address. Compare the spans to street plans, then decide whether to bring back the equipment or answer the unlogged call.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Three crews search for the same kraken egg. Only a nursery with the right currents can keep it alive. Decide which claimant can handle it before opening the reef barrier the crews all need.

name: The head argues with the hands

gm.title: At the table
lines: The walking creature's head wants to surrender. Its hands keep packing stolen goods. Ask the players which part to address and what they can offer both.

name: The hearing is held in two queues

gm.title: At the table
lines: Neighbors have been instructed to stand in different lines outside the same public office. Each line is told the other is petitioning for something it opposes. Both sets of slips carry the same routing stamp. The clerk can show which officer rerouted them after recording both groups’ actual demands.

name: The heir's setting has a hidden pin

gm.title: At the table
lines: A will awards a pendant to whoever has the other half of its setting. Two claimants bring convincing copies. Turn them over to find which one carries a locating pin that fits the pendant's concealed socket.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fixer supplies real leads to build trust and tells a rival which leads the party follows. Let the players plant different bait with each contact.

name: The herb patch belonged to a garden

gm.title: At the table
lines: A potent plant grows in neat rows far from homes. Cleared growth reveals a foundation with rain channels that still work.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hill spirit answers questions by sending stones downhill. An old terrace catches stones from only one direction, letting the party distinguish replies.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A heckler picks exactly the fight that would draw a witness out of the square. The party can ignore them and track the witness instead.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wight records local stories without feeding on anyone. The living witnesses want their versions kept out of the graveyard archive.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The staff disappeared years ago, but guests still put payment in trays. The trays ring when an unknown person pays in the same coin as the last proprietor.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The hearth is warm and the bedding dry. Pegs by the door bear the names of people the cabin owner expects to arrive.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A piece of ice feels warm but never melts. It cools as it approaches the larger glacier and warms when taken away.

name: The infirmary inside the old lair

gm.title: At the table
lines: Healers established a refuge inside a former monster's lair. The defenses suppress intrusive magic well enough to stop a curse, but they also cut off the patients' ability to call for help.

name: The inn that leaves no ashes

gm.title: At the table
lines: Night guests receive exactly the bed they had years before, though the building later vanishes. Someone has scratched a direction in the ashes outside.

name: The invitation to trade a secret

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tempter offers one accurate secret in exchange for a private name. A public way to verify the claim lets the party stall without agreeing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An intelligence in a sealed vessel builds influence by solving small problems for anyone who carries it. Make its favored repair jobs point to the network it is assembling.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The monarch chooses the last performer without showing their face. A stagehand can tell which booth received real supper.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A key turns up on a dry floor carrying mud from a single city block. The matching lock has been moved several times.

name: The lair is behind the waterfall's echo

gm.title: At the table
lines: Sound returns from a second opening on the other side of the falls. In calm water there is a chance to reach it from below.

name: The landing nearest the pantry has a public chair

gm.title: At the table
lines: A long wizard's stair locks every other floor unless someone is sitting at a staffed landing. Visitors can pay the attendant to keep their seat or arrange a shift with a local student who wants to see one particular delivery.

name: The last dose on the road

gm.title: At the table
lines: A sick passenger knows where to find relief and lacks the strength to reach it. Their friend wants the party to take all of the remaining medicine in case of delay.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tavern has a small ball course in the yard. The last cup swallows every ball, and today it has returned one marked with a missing guest's initials.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tavern always has live music. If the band stops, a sleepy patron hears an earlier performance playing below the boards.

name: The last owner of the armor

gm.title: At the table
lines: A suit carries the voice of a former tyrant. Each favor it asks seems fair in isolation. Give its wearer an explicit chance to refuse when a favor would make the next one easier.

name: The last two beats open the chest

gm.title: At the table
lines: A chest has gemstones set in staff lines. A small hinged cover plays the written phrase once and falls silent on two marked beats. Players can clap, tap the cues, or ask a musician for help.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An echo gives away the last word of the creature's next sentence. An interpreter who notices the pattern can use it to tell a threat from a warning.

name: The lending room takes wing at noon

gm.title: At the table
lines: A colony of moths normally keeps scraps of one ruined book in overlapping pockets of its nest. At noon the insects move together to a warmer wall. Paper tabs can mark the scraps the party needs to photograph or copy before the insects resettle.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A long-missing friend sends a letter offering to pay the town's debts. Their old handwriting spells a place name only when the first letters are read down.

name: The librarian answers with a shelf address

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tall caretaker will only move books between one approved room and a fixed desk. The party can place a conflicting catalog slip on the desk to learn where an inaccessible volume was moved, then request a reading witness.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hidden library lends a volume to anyone who brings a local fact nobody has written down. Someone is trading the addresses of witnesses.

name: The lift has weight for a single trip

gm.title: At the table
lines: A powered lift has one descent left before its counterweight must be reset from below. Let the players send a scout, ride down together, or lower supplies first. Show a reachable hand crank on a side landing so a separated group can reunite without depending on a single check.

name: The lights go out at shoulder height

gm.title: At the table
lines: A path through tall luminous fungi has a dark strip where passing travelers touched the stalks. The surviving lights show where they started ducking.

name: The lock reads a path through its alphabet

gm.title: At the table
lines: A floor of letter tiles opens a door when crossed in the order of a phrase shown on a nearby lintel. Mark each correct tile with a harmless audible click. A wrong turn resets the latch and leaves the last correct tile lit.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Time passes slowly in a café open for one outside hour. Make two clocks visible so players can use the respite while a deadline approaches outside.

name: The lookout is protecting a louder room

gm.title: At the table
lines: A guard keeps stepping out of cover to stop tools rattling in the next room. The crew can reveal a bypass if approached before the guard's relief arrives. Pick whether the guard is hiding the crew from their own commander or concealing the work from visitors.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Scouts on a ruler's payroll are afraid to say they lost the road. Their notebooks can still establish where the road used to go.

name: The lost traveler reads from the other bank

gm.title: At the table
lines: An insectfolk traveler carries a map everyone assumes is upside down. Their legend is accurate when read from the far side of the river.

name: The low bidder offered to do half the work

gm.title: At the table
lines: A guild needs the flood marks measured and its old records reconciled. A cheap bid offers only the fieldwork. Players may take the other half, insist on getting the complete brief, or find which result the guild wants to suppress.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Vendors will sell an oddity only in exchange for an errand of equal trouble. They give receipts commemorating bargains customers have forgotten.

gm.title: At the table
lines: During a ball, masks let slip what their owners want. An attendee brings a spare mask hoping it will talk about a previous wearer.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A labyrinth below town corresponds to forgotten surface lots. Use rent rolls to navigate where street names give no clue.

name: The merchant asks after the stock they never sold

gm.title: At the table
lines: A retired merchant knows the party bought from the shop after it changed hands. Their predictions about what should have been on the back shelf are correct, except for an item bought after the transfer. Find where the newer proprietor kept it and why it was moved.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Shooting stars appear only on one side of a ridge. A shepherd has been timing the flashes against lights in a distant tower.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Its eyes and mouth creep toward whichever side of its body is warmest. A hearth draws its attention away from an occupied doorway.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A deserted mine rings its old shift bell. The party can lower a lamp and watch ash blow out of a shaft recorded as sealed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Divine healing temporarily tires the person who grants it. The temple can share the burden, but each faction wants to decide whose cases take priority.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A golem repairs itself inside intact mirrors. Its reflection appears before it steps out. Covering mirrors cuts off escape without destroying evidence etched into their backs.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A mirror reflects everything except the person who purchased it. The secondhand dealer can use it to recognize someone they claim never entered.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A secret ceremony mistakes the party for expected recruits. Listening to the welcoming speech reveals the recruits' actual destination.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A small patch of fog moves travelers sideways while they face forward. Stakes tied to a line make the shift measurable.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A traveler arrives with a witness to a pledge a character may have made. Offer a chance to dispute its terms or find a peaceful settlement.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An hour after breaking camp, the same traveler says the same greeting. An ink mark made during the first encounter can reveal what survived the loop.

name: The nest has a cool rack separate from the hoard

gm.title: At the table
lines: Egg minders keep old nests at different temperatures and move them as the weather turns. The plainest rack contains the most valuable brood. Players who learn the markings can ask for a meeting away from the nursery or carry a crate to a safer shelf.

name: The new rune fits an old mold

gm.title: At the table
lines: A harmless mark shines on the drinker's palm. One workshop uses the same mark inside a form for recognizing approved couriers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An official adds a charge to every receipt the party sees. A second copy of the schedule has the same figures written in different units.

name: The night witness is paid to sleep

gm.title: At the table
lines: A witness to a series of crimes is offered a remarkably comfortable room outside town. The booking register explains who paid for it.

name: The nighttime washer returns a cup for each borrowed drop

gm.title: At the table
lines: It borrows water from a household's stored pots and replaces it later in small cups. It leaves the cups on numbered tiles that mark each pot’s shelf position. A cup alone on one tile shows which pot the washer could not find when returning the water.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A host wants the party at dinner and has set a place for someone they recently crossed. The seating plan tells the party the order in which requests will be made.

name: The official can sign a receipt and nothing else

gm.title: At the table
lines: A clerk has authority to acknowledge a delivery but cannot authorize its storage. When the original keeper misses a shift, show what the party gains by having a receipt and which open question still needs the absent official.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A temple runs the bar and reserves one cask for ceremonies. The last priest authorized to tap it has been barred from the building.

name: The old rival arrives without an audience

gm.title: At the table
lines: An adversary asks the party to negotiate far from witnesses. Agree on which third party will hold the resulting promise.

gm.title: At the table
lines: One chair gives the drinker the bartender's full attention. Everybody else must queue outside where rival petitioners can hear enough to offer deals.

name: The only public anchor is in a private yard

gm.title: At the table
lines: River boats can wait safely at one mooring. A household claims the road crossbar also grants control of the mooring. Compare municipal paving marks to the river charter before the current drives another boat downstream.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Insults spoken on stage often pass for jokes. A nervous guest hires the party to identify the one person the emcee never mocks.

name: The ordinary stock is going to a relief effort

gm.title: At the table
lines: A vendor has promised most of one mundane category to neighbors repairing damage. Let players buy a small personal quantity or negotiate for more by offering delivery or supplies. The merchant calls in the favor even if the party buys nothing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The magistrate who pays restitution also funds the damage. Put the same clerk's distinctive corrections on both sets of books.

name: The parade cuts across a deadline

gm.title: At the table
lines: Floats shut the shortest route to the courthouse. The parade captain can open a gap, but every pause changes the timing of a performance.

name: The pawn clock ran while the shop was shut

gm.title: At the table
lines: A borrower was allowed until noon to recover a case. The shop remained closed for a nearby funeral, but the auction of unclaimed goods still starts at dusk. Use the funeral bell records and morning tally to request more time or help arrange a bid.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An invisible guardian becomes visible at the top of a swinging weight's arc. Players can jam the swing there or release the weight to clear a path.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Street actors improvise around a set of names supplied by the audience. Their scripts change when one late arrival drops a token in the hat.

name: The plush beast has the right anatomy

gm.title: At the table
lines: A handmade toy depicts a creature unknown locally, including an accurate extra joint. Ask who supplied its maker with a model.

name: The posse with an open warrant

gm.title: At the table
lines: A posse wants a missing person found alive. Its warrant gives a second person the authority to call off the pursuit.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A claimant remembers traps in a vanished palace no map records. Someone can verify the details, but only by opening a passage the town relies on staying shut.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two public rivals secretly share responsibility for a ward. Force them to agree on the ward's safety while the party is present.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A public magic contest awards a relic claimed by the family that made it. Contestants can compete to win it for the family or make the dispute public.

name: The purse in a marked tree

gm.title: At the table
lines: Someone left money in a branch deliberately bent over the path. An identical empty branch points back toward the village.

name: The queen pays hunters to return living game

gm.title: At the table
lines: The court's feast celebrates many failed hunts. Each hunter gets a share for a live animal and loses it for a carcass. An envoy wants to pass the stablemaster’s tame boar off as a captured wild one. They need the reward to commission a search for two overdue scouts.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Coral has grown in the exact outline of a faction's emblem. Tracing its growth shows the emblem lay on the reef long before the faction was founded.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An undead pursuer announces exactly when it will next confront its target. Finding out what happened at the previous appointment gives the party leverage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Entry requires copying a drummer's pattern. A courier hides an extra beat in a pattern the owner already knows.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A landmark emerges above the mist. Its alignment shows the official chart swapped the names of two valleys.

gm.title: At the table
lines: People sleeping inside a ring wake in each other's bedrolls with the same gear laid out as before. Whoever stayed on watch can describe what moved and when.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A voyager sketches a map with a river running uphill. A local lockkeeper recognizes the markings as instructions for a gate the town sealed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A traveler arrives by magic, checks a carved mark, and waits. They have to decide whether to risk a return spell after seeing the mark rubbed away.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Novices train on an uncovered bluff where winter storms pass through every classroom. A sealed guest room would keep travelers safe, but the keeper refuses to open it until somebody can account for the last people inside.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A seer predicts burning rain. Quarry workers can roof the market or brace the granary before dusk and need help doing both.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hollow stone sack carries a folded strap worn like cloth. The local mason can identify the quarry by pockets inside the hollow.

name: The safe step is the apparent drop

gm.title: At the table
lines: An obvious gap draws attention away from an unstable landing. Let a tossed stone tip the landing and reveal a broad step inside the first gap. The party can use that step, brace the landing with magic, or cross above both.

name: The safest room gives away the route

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wax seal closes a shelter against a passing hazard. Each opening leaves a crease that a pursuer can count. The party can unseal it for someone outside, leave a deliberate false count, or take the exposed way and reserve the refuge for others.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Small kitchen dragons won't heat iron that crossed a ward. A cook can test the party's confiscated kit while dinner is on.

name: The salvage camp is built for different hands

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every tool has a tall grip but the camp has small footprints. A low ramp and a set of counterweights let smaller workers use giant equipment. Learn the rhythm of the yard and the party can help remove material trapping a wagon.

name: The salvage crane makes the fight move

gm.title: At the table
lines: A crane swings a dangling cargo net across three floor bays whenever its exposed wheel turns. Anyone can crank it, wedge it, or cut the load loose. Put one valuable crate and one trapped worker in different bays so choosing where the net lands matters.

gm.title: At the table
lines: After a god dies, fading texts leave rival temples with different surviving verses. Give a third copy to someone who needs the party's help to preserve it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tail vanishes from an alley but leaves wet prints leading into a crowded bakery. There are three exits and bakers know who used each.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Dolphins follow the ship in two ranks. One rank veers toward every bad plank that leaks. A sailor can watch the pattern to find a slow leak without unloading the hold.

name: The second-in-command is trained for a different month

gm.title: At the table
lines: The deputy practiced the winter duties, but only the summer records survive. They need a witness to confirm which procedure applies now. The players can find the witness or ask for a temporary rule with an expiration date.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each patron gets seeds for the birds. The flock sorts them by size and carries the largest to a damaged vent outside.

name: The seed parcel that came back

gm.title: At the table
lines: Seeds arrive from plants known to propagate another way. Their packet carries the return address of a gardener who buys failed experiments.

name: The seller will demonstrate it twice

gm.title: At the table
lines: A magic goods vendor will give two trials using shop equipment. The customer chooses the test conditions and keeps any pictures or readings it produces. A successful trial proves exactly what the trial showed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Dragon-shaped shadows cross town against the wind. From the tower the party can see nobody casts them, but the shadows follow a marked route.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shell always whispers the same small amount at the same tide. The old harbor tariff lists who was bound to pay it.

name: The shop trades favors in fixed increments

gm.title: At the table
lines: Give the merchant three favors with stated scale and payoff. Buying ordinary stock still costs coins. Specialty stock can be reserved by doing one favor, and the customer may dislodge the reservation by asking for a cash-only price.

name: The short route has one drawback

gm.title: At the table
lines: Someone offers a route that cuts half a day off the trek. They only walked it while the sluice was open.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A novice boasts about a unique find. The object has an inventory number that belongs to the local museum's current display.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wrecked sanctuary sits over the remains of an earlier one. Identifying the gods by their orientations lets players find the concealed approach.

name: The signet leaves an absent shape

gm.title: At the table
lines: Wax under a featureless signet sheds all dust except over the place a design should be. The signet's maker asks whether the original was filed off or never present.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A procession asks each witness to carry an empty lantern one block. Each willing hand moves the group one house closer to a grave with no name.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A singer's chorus puts people to sleep only when it echoes back. Mark the walls creating that echo and find who chose the route.

name: The sketch has a future repair

gm.title: At the table
lines: A drawing of a character includes gear as it would look after an unusual repair. The local craftsperson can quote the price and say who ordered it.

name: The skirmish had a third line

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two groups left signs of fighting. A third trail from baggage carts reveals somebody else took the supplies.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An undead tradesperson remembers an alchemy commission through its costs. Give the party three invoices and let the skull identify which one names an impossible delivery.

name: The smell from the dyer's cart

gm.title: At the table
lines: A splash on a stolen length of cloth leaves an odor one kennel can track across town. The dyer will lend work clothes in exchange for the return of the original bolt.

name: The spare mount for a messenger

gm.title: At the table
lines: A rider's mount collapses just short of town. Sending the message ahead requires borrowing a riding animal from a reluctant teamster.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fresh-looking carcass is recorded in an inventory made three generations ago. Its wound suggests someone has removed a piece quite recently.

name: The spell that lost its owner

gm.title: At the table
lines: An orphan spell jumps between objects made of the same wood. Identify that timber by watching where it stops.

name: The stall confirms reservations only by noon

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two customers request the last batch. The merchant records whose deposit arrived first but allows that buyer until noon to collect. The party can ask to see an example, wait, or make a separate batch possible by bringing the remaining ingredient.

name: The stall has an exit clause

gm.title: At the table
lines: A seller agrees in writing to exchange a delicate specialty item within a day if its effect fails under one agreed condition. Write down who will judge the test and what the exchange is worth. The seller can earn repeat business by honoring it in a difficult case.

name: The stars on the other side

gm.title: At the table
lines: A star chart matches no current sky. A widely traveled navigator can identify the view as a reflected sky from the opposite hemisphere.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A pickpocket takes one glove and ignores money. Wet ink from a forged signature is still inside the cuff. Once it dries, the forger can scrape most of it off.

name: The stomach hides a traveling route

gm.title: At the table
lines: The stones in a cave predator's gizzard were rounded by a fast stream. A geologist can use their colors to pick out the route the creature takes between caves.

name: The stone fisher lets coins pass

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cave predator drops coins and jewels because it hunts only things that move under their own power. Slide a weighted sample down the entrance before deciding where to go.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A stone egg is cold on top and warm underneath. Local birds add nesting material around it even when it is moved.

name: The stone key sets a weight

gm.title: At the table
lines: A huge stone key is much heavier than a person can turn by hand. Its teeth match wedges in a counterweight slot.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Its joints petrify in direct sun. Tracks stop at a bright patch and resume on the far side after dark. Move the shade to bring it out or let it cross unharmed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The sunset match is fought by volunteers for the right to pour the last drink. A losing visitor is desperate to remain inside after closing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guests point out an animal for the kitchen. One of the pens has a nameplate meant for a person expected at the table that evening.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two neighbors wake in each other's bodies. Each has a duty the other refuses to perform and needs a neutral witness to an agreement.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Half the people at a feast fall ill. The servers brought special dishes to the seats with blue cards, and someone swapped those cards after place settings were laid.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Let players who like solving problems see the opponent's constraints before risking a resource. Put an exception somewhere they can investigate and use if they choose.

name: The tattoo sets a limit the wearer can show

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bearer holds up a hand to indicate how many strangers they can still escort through a warded gate today. The bars fade one at a time when someone crosses with them. Give the bearer a reason to reserve the last place and the travelers a way to stay safely outside.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A passage under a cellar leads to a crypt door. The brewery's seepage has started to erase pictograms showing which stones are safe to lift.

name: The toad follows the newest footprints

gm.title: At the table
lines: A toad in the hag's sitting room wears a ruined adventurer's boot buckle. It will retrace the route to their gear if somebody places the buckle on the floor.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A private dining room seals until the dessert is shared equally. Someone interrupts dinner to flee and leaves one seat unclaimed.

name: The tower’s upper floor returns to the same hour

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each ascent arrives at the start of the same upper-floor hour. Each descent returns to the start of the next hour downstairs. The courier remembers what happens during every visit and can deliver a message to a worker who starts the hour without it.

name: The town pays in returned favors for an afternoon

gm.title: At the table
lines: People redeem favors posted last year at particular stalls. Let players redeem a small favor from an ally, post a new obligation under clear terms, or investigate an ancient claim someone brought out to interrupt the festival.

name: The tune that closes a wound

gm.title: At the table
lines: A singer can close a wound with the right verse. The verse names whoever inflicted it, which matters when the patient begs for privacy.

name: The two-tailed fox barters for shelter

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fox can hide itself and one small object under the curl of each tail. It wants protection for a night and lets the party choose which of two objects to return to their apparent owners.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Armored ghosts walk to the same unnamed graves each night. A mason has a list of names left off the memorial.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Cattle disappear without breaking the paddock gate. Their bells can still be heard beneath the floor of the dairy.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The dummy calls out the amount each patron owes. Its performer insists the dummy has started quoting figures from an account neither can see.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A title keeps a magical protection active whenever the villain answers to it. A witness who knows their given name can call them away from their audience and ask to speak as old neighbors.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old statue stands behind thick vines. A worn plaque distinguishes the depicted person from the modern hero locals name.

name: The wagon the owner left behind

gm.title: At the table
lines: Cargo remains in an overturned cart wrapped for rain. Someone repaired the axle and then left without moving it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Dirt and hair float around it as though submerged. Watch what drifts toward it to find the concealed drain it uses as a den.

name: The wall closes on the wrong room

gm.title: At the table
lines: A lever marked for rescue closes a stone partition through enchanted force. Chisel marks show where it comes down. An inscription on the other side identifies a release the trapped character can reach with light.

name: The walls defend the old map

gm.title: At the table
lines: Forgotten walls animate when they detect a threat. They defend the historical boundaries, leaving the newer district outside.

name: The water crop fails at one ledge

gm.title: At the table
lines: Empty barrelstalks mark one level of a cavern. Higher shelves still yield water. A local grower asks the party to identify what drained the low shelf before the next planting.

name: The weigh house keeps two sets of stones

gm.title: At the table
lines: Public and private stones have the same numbered units. The public stones weigh more and entitle grant holders to more grain. A grant receipt bears the private stamp and understates the amount owed. Put both one-unit stones on opposite pans to prove the shortfall.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Patrons get a meal discount for lifting a heavy keg. One keg feels lighter each day and never sounds empty.

name: The witness at the wrong angle

gm.title: At the table
lines: A fatal blow lands in a public arcade. A mirror above a shutter gives the party a chance to contradict two confident witnesses.

name: The witness resents where the party put their chair

gm.title: At the table
lines: Someone told them to speak from the accused person's side of the room before anyone asked their account. When they meet the party again, they ask for a place to talk that doesn't imply allegiance. Give them one location where both groups will recognize them.

name: The witness saw the lantern go out from above

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two accounts agree a lantern failed but disagree on who was near it. A service hatch frames the lantern while concealing the platform below. Replaying each witness's position determines which account can place a person at the scene. Leave the reason for the outage open until the party inspects the wick.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A grove begins growing around recently moved fences. The families that moved them can settle the dispute or wait to see which field the grove claims.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shop runs tools without staff every night. The new owner wants to rent the benches as they are and the previous owner left a stop order.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A witness recognizes the crest on a borrowed coat and swears the wearer inherited a debt. The party can return the coat or investigate who planted it.

name: Three merchants sell shade in the same yard

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each leases a shadow from a different roof. At midday their leases overlap on the only cool patch. The party can buy time to treat someone overheated, renegotiate the hour, or help raise public canvas in the street.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An enormous goose has claimed a bridge and collects polished buttons. A rivet from the ruined railing can draw it away while someone reinforces the weak planks.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Tiny clockwork trains deliver drinks. A passenger asks to borrow the spare track to send a note past a guard who checks every server.

name: Track one supply that can run short

gm.title: At the table
lines: Before departure, pick one supply scarce on this route and state which hazard consumes it. Give an approximate cost in time or risk for two known ways to resupply. Keep incidental expenses out of this count.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Orchard keepers plant saplings across a proposed city wall. A surveyor will accept their claim if someone finds an older drainage map.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Mounted riders accuse a ship of crossing a boundary. The ship stayed on its declared course. The tritons can show that the marker stones moved after the latest tide.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Trolls serve tea after collecting the bridge toll. A regular knows which herb signals that the bridge is unsafe and who taught the trolls to use it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Anyone can talk safely inside the inn after surrendering arms. A bell tells everyone when a surrendered item is moved, including the one a guest needs to get home.

name: Two apprentices inherit the same unfinished tattoo

gm.title: At the table
lines: A retired artist drew half a commemorative piece before losing their steady hand. Each apprentice can complete a different missing part. The client must choose whether to keep it unfinished, share the commission, or accept one drawing that changes its meaning.

name: Two caches hold the same key blank

gm.title: At the table
lines: A key in a flooded lockbox and another in a dry wall cavity share their cut but have different maker's marks. Trying either at the gate works. Comparing the marks can show who copied the lock before the authorities replaced it, which changes who can be trusted to guard it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An heir and a jeweler each have paperwork for the same valuable ring. One document claims the metal and the other the stone.

name: Two drip trays date a switch

gm.title: At the table
lines: Red and white candles were lit together over numbered trays. A fireman opened a service hatch halfway through the watch, sending both flames sideways. The party can compare the order of straight and sideways wax streaks to tell whether the labeled trays were switched before or after the hatch opened.

name: Two fair winds meet on a saddle

gm.title: At the table
lines: Winds blow toward the same saddle from opposite valleys. The dry grass shows the boundary shifting during the day. A caravan with a sail-powered cart can wait for the winds to line up with the descent or furl the sail and haul the cart down with ropes.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A noble's death is celebrated at one gate and mourned at another. Each procession believes theirs has the body.

name: Two neighborhood contests share one prize

gm.title: At the table
lines: One crowd awards the trophy for the fastest completion, and the other for the tidiest work. The same carpenter is judging both. Let the party choose which standard to endorse or build another trophy instead of taking the first.

name: Two plans contradict an architect’s alibi

gm.title: At the table
lines: A Plan-reader lamp flickers at different doorways on each submitted plan. One drawing gives someone a route from the street past the locked entrance. Ask who paid for the intervening renovation, or try the route before the owner notices the check.

name: Two rival associations pay for the same footpath

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each pays for a different half and saws through its posts when the other falls behind. A flood has temporarily shifted the midpoint. The party can broker shared upkeep or learn where the joint account still has funds.

name: Two satyrs disagree about the joke

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two performers have wagered something they cannot afford to lose. A party member can judge fairly or find a target both would rather tease.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Rival bars each brew one half of a drink. Both halves must reach the bridge before the ferryman opens the crossing, and tonight the brewers are feuding.

name: Two tattoo portraits disagree about the span

gm.title: At the table
